title: RecordingTool evidence window reopened for self-guarding tools (yaah-qlli follow-up)
description: Because guard-routed tools implement selfGuardsPath, RecordingTool no longer holds the per-path lock across its before-snapshot / inner.Execute / after-snapshot sequence (it cannot: the lock is not reentrant). The before-snapshot now runs outside the tool's critical section, so a concurrent dispatch's write can be attributed to the wrong dispatch — the exact misattribution the wrapper lock existed to prevent. Diagnosis quality only; bytes stay correct. Fix: an onCommit hook inside withFileWrite that records the after-snapshot from the receipt digest while the lock is still held. Related simplification: replace holds its whole candidate path set across a recursive walk; per-file withFileWrite gives identical semantics with O(1) hold time and removes replaceFileLocked's unenforced 'caller holds the set' contract.

title: resolveProvider silently falls back and mislabels the provider in errors
description:
## Problem

When `agents.default.provider` names a provider that is unusable (e.g. missing/unresolved API key), `resolveProvider()` silently falls back to the first provider by sorted name that has a usable credential, while `resolveProviderName()` still returns the configured name. The session's provider instance and provider name then disagree.

Observed 2026-11-12: config had `agents.default.provider: qwen-token-plan` with `api_key: ${DASHSCOPE_API_KEY}`. The TUI process did not have DASHSCOPE_API_KEY in its environment (it had QWEN_API_KEY / BAILIAN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY), so the provider was unusable. Requests were sent to DeepSeek's base URL with model `qwen3.8-max`, producing:

```
provider error [qwen-token-plan/qwen3.8-max]: bad request format — abort: provider returned 400: The supported API model names are deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, but you passed qwen3.8-max.
```

The label named qwen-token-plan and the model named qwen3.8-max, but the endpoint was api.deepseek.com. The same pattern produced `provider error [deepseek/GLM-5.3]` in traces.

## Where

- `cmd/yaah/wiring_stages.go:103-105` — `provider: resolveProvider(cfg)` and `providerName: resolveProviderName(cfg)` resolved independently.
- `cmd/yaah/provider_resolve.go:422` (`resolveProvider`) — silent alphabetical fallback.
- `cmd/yaah/provider_resolve.go:145` (`resolveProviderName`) — returns the configured name regardless of whether the provider is usable.

## Expected

1. `resolveProvider` should emit a loud `slog.Warn` when the configured provider is unusable and it falls back, naming the configured provider and the fallback actually used (the sub-agent path already does this via `resolveSubAgent`).
2. The reported provider name should follow the provider instance actually used (or the resolved pair should be returned together) so error labels, TUI header, and prompts cannot claim a different endpoint than the one serving the request.

## Repro

```bash
env -u DASHSCOPE_API_KEY yaah -- 'say hi in one word'
# provider error [qwen-token-plan/qwen3.8-max]: ... api.deepseek.com 400 ...
```

With DASHSCOPE_API_KEY set the same command succeeds.

## Notes

Root cause of the user's immediate failure was the env var name (config references ${DASHSCOPE_API_KEY}, process had QWEN_API_KEY / BAILIAN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY). This bead is for the misleading silent-fallback/mislabeling behaviour, which made the root cause hard to see.

description: Groups the unorganized beads-tooling beads: prevent bd github sync from re-filing existing issues (zrv7, P1 — root cause of the 22 timestamp-ID duplicate beads closed 2026-11-13), repair the local beads workspace (gvk), native bead tool (mpln).

title: move/copy are unguarded on the orchestrator lane (yaah-qlli follow-up)
description: The per-path lock for transfers lives only in RecordingTool (recording.go recordTransfer), which wraps sub-agent dispatch roles only. An orchestrator-lane copy/move therefore does a bare read-then-write with no lock and no CAS: it can silently revert a concurrent sub-agent write that landed in between — the same lost-update class yaah-qlli fixed elsewhere, one tool family over. Fix: move the {src,dst} set acquisition into MoveTool/CopyTool.Execute, add selfGuardsPath, and make recordTransfer skip its own lock for marked tools. Secondary: bulk_files' mutating loop takes no lock or CAS at all, and fileguard.go names it as covered.

feat(workflow): propose command with bounded repair loop
description:
## Problem

A model should be able to author a workflow, but an invalid spec must not run
and a repair loop must be bounded.

## Scope

- `yaah workflow propose "<intent>"`: an orchestrator dispatch that emits a
  spec.
- Strict schema validation with a bounded repair loop (max 3), targeting stable
  WF codes.
- Dry-run/explain the result before returning it.
- Never execute the spec; execution requires explicit approval.
- Tests with the deterministic provider and invalid-spec fixtures.

## Design

- One dispatch role, not a new planner runtime.
- The repair loop feeds diagnostics back to the model; no infinite retries.
- The output is a spec file/content plus its validation/explain summary.
- Self-modification gate: propose -> validate -> explain -> policy -> run.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(workflow): opt-in workflow_run tool with approval gate
description:
## Problem

The orchestrator can author a spec, but executing it from the model loop must be
opt-in and gated.

## Scope

- Opt-in `workflow_run` tool: spec content/path, params, dry-run flag.
- Validate -> explain -> approval-policy check -> execute.
- Refuse execution when validation fails or approval is denied.
- Trace/audit every decision.
- Tool schema, prompt doc, and config gating.
- Tests for denied and approved paths.

## Design

- The tool is an adapter over the executor; no second scheduler.
- Default off; enabling it is an explicit config choice.
- The model proposes; the runtime disposes.
- Dry-run returns the explain output without executing.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(workflow): render command, template gallery, and metrics
description:
## Problem

A graph is easier to review visually, and the project needs adoption metrics
that show whether the DSL is working.

## Scope

- `yaah workflow render <spec> --format mermaid|html` from the resolved IR,
  read-only.
- Template gallery/examples for common shapes.
- Metrics: invalid-spec rate, repair attempts, spec-vs-actual trace diff.
- Tests for deterministic output.
- No visual editor.

## Design

- Render from the IR, not from YAML text; the graph is the source of truth.
- HTML is a static, self-contained artifact.
- Metrics are derived from traces; no new telemetry pipeline.
- Read-only: `render` never executes.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(workflow): call subworkflows with registry and depth limits
description:
## Problem

Reusable subworkflows are useful, but file-path includes are a path-traversal
and versioning risk.

## Scope

- `call` node: `workflow`, `params`, `max_depth`.
- Named subworkflow registry plus an explicit `--workflow-root`.
- Path containment checks; no `./sub.yaml` escapes.
- Depth limit and call-graph cycle detection in validation.
- Budget/fan-out expansion includes call expansion.
- Tests for traversal, depth, and parameter passing.

## Design

- Registry allowlist, not free-form paths.
- A called workflow is validated and resolved like the root.
- `max_depth` is bounded and enforced by the validator and runtime.
- No implicit network or filesystem access from a called spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(workflow): workflow-level on_abort dispositions
description:
## Problem

When a run aborts, open proposals can leak. The workflow needs an explicit
disposition policy.

## Scope

- Workflow-level `on_abort: halt | release_all | discard_all` (default `halt`).
- On abort, apply the policy to every open proposal created by the run.
- Integrate with `yaah shepherd prune` as a safety net, not the primary
  mechanism.
- Assert zero open proposals after `release_all`/`discard_all`.
- Tests for abort during fan-out, settle, and resume.

## Design

- Use the existing settlement path; no new cleanup engine.
- `halt` is loud and leaves cleanup to the operator/prune.
- The validator requires `on_abort` when any proposal may remain open.
- Record every abort disposition in the trace.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(workflow): replay mode and resume idempotency hardening
description:
## Problem

The deterministic skeleton should be testable and reproducible without model
calls, and resume must be idempotent under crashes.

## Scope

- `yaah workflow run --replay <run_id>` substitutes recorded agent outputs.
- Deterministic skeleton runs with no model calls.
- Resume idempotency: kill points, duplicate settle refused, no duplicate
  dispatch.
- Trace-backed replay equivalence tests.
- Property tests for crash/resume sequences.

## Design

- Replay reads the same trace records the executor writes; no separate replay
  format.
- Recorded outputs are keyed by node id + item key + attempt.
- Replay refuses when a required output is missing; no silent regeneration.
- The spec hash must match.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: feat(workflow): adversarial security suite for untrusted specs
description:
## Problem

A workflow file is untrusted input. The parser and validator must fail closed
against escalation, cost bombs, and traversal.

## Scope

- Oversized specs, node counts, prompt bytes, template depth.
- Role escalation, grant widening, overlapping grants, world escapes.
- Cost bombs: fanout × loop × call expansion, concurrency bombs.
- Path traversal in `call`; prompt-size bombs; inline secrets.
- Prompt-injection boundaries in spec text and interpolated report values.
- Fuzz/property tests for decoder and validator.
- Document the threat model in `docs/workflows.md`.

## Design

- Allowlists for roles, subworkflows, asserts, selector functions, and aggregate
  strategies.
- Spec may narrow but never widen host-configured maximums.
- Every rejection has a stable WF code and a node path.
- No ambient authority: the spec cannot read files, run shell, or call arbitrary
  tools.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: docs(workflow): five bench tasks and docs/workflows.md
description:
## Problem

One bench task proves the concept; five prove the semantics, and users need a
reference.

## Scope

- Five `orch-*` tasks pass from specs: `orch-settle-discard`, `orch-guard`,
  `orch-quality-gate`, `orch-escalation`, `orch-recovery`.
- `docs/workflows.md`: user guide + reference (syntax, node kinds, validation
  codes, security, CLI, examples).
- Update `docs/features.md` and the parity/scorecard docs where they claim
  orchestration coverage.
- At least one real workflow beyond the bench (dependency upgrade or repo-wide
  refactor), documented.
- Examples checked in and validated by CI.

## Design

- Do not overfit to bench tasks; the real workflow is evidence of pull.
- Docs state behavior and policy, not duplicated schema argument semantics.
- No new documentation framework; plain Markdown.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Persist finished background-job records across restart so subagent_jobs never reports a finished job as unknown
description:
## Problem

yaah-was9.1 shipped the universal completion envelope and subagent_jobs status/wait now surface a bounded result + result_available for terminal jobs — but job records live only in the in-memory Manager. After a process restart, a finished job's record is gone: subagent_jobs reports status=unknown with a caveat note ('a job record that disappeared', internal/prompts/tools/subagent_jobs.md:30). The docs disclose the loss; they do not prevent it. yaah-was9.1's note ('a restart should not silently lose a finished job's record') is the one item its audit found unimplemented.

## Scope

• Persist terminal job snapshots (id, role, description/model/world, status, bounded result, duration_ms) in the same store family as sessions, keyed by session.
• On Manager construction, rehydrate finished records for the session so status/wait return the envelope-backed result instead of unknown.
• Keep in-flight (non-terminal) jobs restart-scoped: only terminal records survive.
• Bound storage (TTL or per-session cap) so long-lived sessions don't accumulate.
• Tests: deliver → restart → status returns the record; unknown still correct for never-dispatched ids.

## Seams

• internal/jobs/manager.go (terminal snapshot + rehydrate)
• the session store family in internal/memory (or the session record itself)
• internal/tools/subagent_jobs.go (unchanged surface; unknown narrows)

## Out of scope

• Resuming in-flight work; replaying Deliver for jobs delivered pre-restart (delivered records may be pruned per the TTL rule).

title: EPIC: declarative workflow DSL over dispatch and proposal settlement
description:
# Declarative workflow DSL over dispatch and proposal settlement

## Summary

Add a declarative workflow DSL (`yaah.workflow/v1`) as a thin front-end over the
existing dispatch, retained-proposal, and settlement primitives. A workflow is a
reviewable YAML/JSON artifact with a fixed node vocabulary, bounded loops,
first-class proposals, and static authority/cost analysis. The executor is
host-side, calls the same typed dispatch/settlement core as the model-facing
tools, and is not retained (repo decision D8).

## Why

Today an orchestration is a performance. The operator prompts, watches turns,
copy-pastes diffs, and the process lives in their head and in a chat thread. The
DSL turns a recurring chore into an artifact the team owns: validate, explain,
run. The differentiator is settlement, not syntax: every branch ends in a
reviewable proposal with exactly one disposition.

## Scope

- `internal/workflow/{spec,ir,validate,exec,bind,trace}` plus
  `cmd/yaah/workflow.go`.
- PR 0: extract typed `dispatch.Run` and `dispatch.Settle` from the
  model-facing tool bodies so tools and executor share one core.
- P0: spec/schema/hash, IR/selectors/templates, validators WF001–WF036,
  `validate`/`explain` CLI, golden specs, accepted decisions.
- P1: deterministic scheduler, `delegate`/`emit`, proposal/`settle`, fan-out
  (`join: all`), `loop`/`branch`/`aggregate`, SQLite resume, trace records, one
  end-to-end bench task.
- P2: `join: any|quorum`, `select`, `gate`, `human`, `call`, workflow-level
  `on_abort`, replay/idempotency, security suite, five bench tasks + docs.
- P3: `workflow propose`, opt-in `workflow_run` tool, `workflow render` +
  metrics.

## Non-goals

- No expression language, user-defined functions, arbitrary cycles, imports, or
  spec-side I/O.
- No second scheduler, no second settlement path, no new config system.
- No visual editor, cross-harness export, or retained root workflow run.
- No backward-compatibility scaffolding: one `apiVersion`, strict decode,
  delete rather than deprecate.

## Design commitments

- One IR, one executor, fixed `switch node.Kind`; no plugin registry until a
  second implementation exists.
- `settle` has four terminal verbs only (`select|apply|release|discard`);
  `continue`/`fork` are derivation lifecycle actions on `delegate`.
- One state reducer; the trace is a projection. Compile templates and selectors
  at load.
- Every feature needs a passing `orch-*` bench task or a real workflow.
- The spec is untrusted input: fail closed, allowlist roles/subworkflows, and
  never widen the host's configured authority.

## Plan

Full design: `/home/greg/Code/Agentic/Frameworks/yaah-workflow-dsl-plan.md`.
Decisions WD1–WD10 are accepted as part of this epic.

title: docs(workflow): golden specs and orch-* bench mapping
description:
## Problem

The validators and executor need a shared corpus of realistic workflow specs,
and the project needs to prove the IR can express the existing orchestration
bench tasks.

## Scope

- Three golden specs: sequential pipeline, fan-out + settle, bounded repair loop.
- A mapping table from the ten `bench/orchestration-tasks/orch-*` tasks to IR
  constructs (which node kinds, lanes, joins, settlement actions).
- A small script or Go test that validates all goldens.
- Keep the specs in a stable repo location (e.g. `internal/workflow/testdata/`
  or `docs/workflows/`).

## Design

- Goldens are real, readable workflows, not minimal schema dumps.
- The bench mapping is a design check, not a requirement that every task run
  yet.
- No separate "spec DSL" for tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: EPIC: tool contract hardening — typed results, validated contracts, strict arguments
description:
The delegation engine is strong; the weak seam is what the orchestrator may ask for and what it gets back. This epic makes the dispatch/result contract explicit and machine-checkable without adding a new orchestration model.

## Scope

1. **Universal typed result envelope** across proposal, report, shared, background, and error lanes.
2. **Parse and validate the role response contract** (Markdown and JSON), with required/typed fields and a json_mode schema.
3. **Strict argument validation** for `delegate` and `subagent_jobs`: reject unknown fields, surface clamped overrides, validate sizes.

## Out of scope

- A stage/handoff engine or agent-callable persona switch (see `docs/adr` / `.agents/plans/adr/0001-persona-handoff-and-stage-pipelines.md`).
- A batch/wave dispatch tool.
- General DAG/workflow orchestration.

## PR plan

Recommended: **4 PRs**.

1. Strict argument validation (child 3) — small, standalone.
2. Universal envelope for foreground lanes and errors (child 1).
3. Background completion and `subagent_jobs` result visibility on the envelope (child 1).
4. Contract parsing/validation plus json_mode schema/response_format (child 2).

Child 1 is expected to span PRs 2–3; child 2 is PR 4; child 3 is PR 1. A fifth PR is justified only if the json_mode/response_format work is split from contract parsing.

## Why

- The proposal lane returns JSON; report/shared lanes return prose; background returns prefixed text; some failures are JSON and others are Go errors. The orchestrator must branch on lane and parse prose.
- The role response contract is prompt-only. Only `verdict` is parsed, by regex; JSON-mode roles and Markdown gates disagree about the format.
- Unknown tool arguments are silently ignored. A typo such as `backgroud`, `seed_form`, or `max_turn` silently changes behavior instead of failing.

## Success

- Every completed dispatch returns one typed envelope with status, stop reason, contract, evidence, warnings, artifacts, and recovery guidance.
- A declared contract is parsed and validated; missing required fields are reported, and JSON mode produces/validates the same fields.
- Unknown arguments are rejected with an allowed-key list; clamped overrides are visible.
- Existing roles and callers keep working without changes unless they relied on silent typos.

title: Parse and validate subagent response contracts
description:
## Problem

`buildSubAgentSysPrompt` renders the role's response contract as prompt text, but the harness only parses the `verdict` field with a regex (`parseContractVerdict`). Other declared fields are never validated, JSON-mode roles are told to emit a JSON object while shown a Markdown contract, and quality gates fall back to a PASS/FAIL heuristic when the block is absent or JSON.

## Work

- Parse the declared contract block from the final report into a map; support Markdown bullets and JSON.
- Include the parsed contract in the universal result envelope (child 1).
- Extend `ContractField` with `required`, `type` (`string`, `int`, `bool`, `path`, `command`, `url`, `enum`), and `enum`; validate after the run.
- Add a role/contract `on_missing: warn | error` policy. Default `warn` for compatibility; QA/reviewer roles can fail closed.
- Validate `kind` values at role-file load and in the `role` tool.
- For `json_mode`, generate a JSON Schema from the contract and pass it through `response_format` where supported; otherwise validate the JSON after the run.
- Fix the JSON-mode verdict mismatch so quality gates parse the same contract shape they ask for.
- Update `list_subagents` to show required/typed fields.

## Seams

- `internal/rolefile/rolefile.go` (`ContractField`, `ContractDef`)
- `internal/agent/runner/subagent_prompt.go` (contract rendering)
- `internal/agent/runner/task_runner.go` (final report handling)
- `internal/agent/agent_tools.go` (`parseContractVerdict`, gate verdict)
- `internal/tools/list_subagents.go`
- `internal/tools/delegate.go` / result envelope

## Compatibility

Existing role files without `required`/`type` keep working: absent metadata means the historical "expect the field, but only warn" behavior is preserved unless a role opts into `on_missing: error`.

title: Structured result envelopes for action/state tools
description:
## Problem

Result shape is mixed. Structured JSON is used for `diff`, `go_test`, `go_mod`, `staticcheck`, `bisect`, `file_info`, `wait_for`, `watch`, `proposal`, and `delegate`. Action/state tools still return prose: `plan`, `role`, `skill`, `memory_add`/`update`/`delete`/`promote`, `background_process`, and `supervisor` (`list_scopes`/`status`).

Prose is fine for `read`/`grep`/`ls`; it is a loss for state changes and orchestration, where the caller needs a machine-checkable outcome.

## Work

- Add a small envelope for action/state tools, for example `{status, action, data, warnings}`. Reuse the `Outcome` shape where it already exists.
- Apply it to `plan`, `role`, `skill`, `memory_*`, `background_process`, and `supervisor` list/status. Keep simple file primitives as prose.
- Preserve human-readable text in a `summary`/`message` field where useful.
- Add tests asserting the JSON shape and that failures remain Go errors.
- Document which tools are structured and which are prose, and why.

## Acceptance

The listed action/state tools return a stable JSON envelope; state-changing outcomes are machine-checkable; file primitives remain prose by design; docs and tests pin the split.

title: decision: auto-retry a sealed proposal
description:
# Decision: auto-retry a sealed proposal

Deferred until `yaah-ixyx` (safe preflight/report retry) has evidence.

Currently a proposal-lane body failure can still seal a reviewable partial
proposal. Automatically retrying would create a second proposal unless the
failed artifact is explicitly discarded, and consume-once settlement expects
one reviewable artifact per dispatch.

Decide:
- whether auto-retry after seal is ever desirable;
- if yes, how failed proposals are discarded (manifest/worktree/container),
  how attempt IDs are retained, and how the orchestrator sees both attempts;
- whether the default remains "no auto-retry; orchestrator discards and
  re-dispatches".

Acceptance: written decision with lane/lifecycle semantics, settlement impact,
trace evidence, and either an implementation bead or explicit decline.

title: decision: dispatch fallback and recover policies
description:
# Decision: dispatch fallback and recover policies

Deferred until `yaah-ixyx` has evidence. The v1 recommendation is to decline
both as generic combinators:

- `fallback` chains tasks in Python. The yaah equivalent would chain
  roles/prompts/models with different lanes, tool belts, and output contracts;
  the orchestrator can choose a different role after a structured failure.
- `recover` returns a caller-supplied default, which can make a failed
  dispatch look successful. yaah already returns structured failure envelopes
  (`timed out`, `stuck`, `cancelled`) and lets the orchestrator decide.

Decide whether any narrowly useful form exists, for example:
- same-lane role fallback after a retryable failure;
- provider/model fallback (possibly at the provider layer, not dispatch);
- a literal recover result only for report roles.

Acceptance: written decision per concept with lane semantics, failure
classification, and either a scoped implementation bead or explicit decline.

title: decision: preventive dispatch path claims for parallel sub-agents
description:
# Decision: preventive dispatch path claims

Deferred until the conflict model and resolution workflow have real usage data.

The model often does not know its write set before running, so up-front path
claims can create false confidence. Only consider prevention if repeated
overlaps justify it.

Decide whether to add:
- optional `delegate` write-path hints/claims;
- a scheduler that delays or rejects overlapping claims;
- role-level path ownership;
- nothing (keep visibility + resolution as the control).

Acceptance: decision grounded in observed conflict rates/paths; if adopted,
define how claims are declared, validated, released, and reconciled with actual
changes; if declined, record why.

title: feat(conflict): aggregate conflict facts for prevention revisit
description:
# Aggregate conflict facts for the prevention revisit

The `yaah-6xyl.4` decision declines preventive path claims until there is measured evidence, but the current conflict facts are not aggregated:

- `yaah.proposal.conflict.v1` is emitted from `proposal list`/`show`, deduped per registry, not at seal/detection time; proposals that are never inspected have no fact.
- There is no total fan-out/dispatch denominator, so "conflicts per fan-out" cannot be computed.
- There is no rollup of repeated path pairs or resolution cost.

## Scope

- Define a small aggregate view over conflict facts: sessions with conflicts, conflict kind counts, conflicting path pairs, and proposal fan-out denominator.
- Ensure conflict evidence is recorded when detected, not only when the orchestrator happens to call list/show.
- Make repeated-path metrics path-based, not proposal-id-based (proposal ids are per-process).
- Include `same_path_divergent`, `delete_modify`, `parent_overlap`, and `path_overlap`; keep duplicates separate.
- Add a report/query path sufficient to evaluate the revisit criteria in `docs/conflict-prevention-decision.md`.
- No path claims, scheduler, or role ownership in this bead; this is measurement only.

## Acceptance

A report can answer, over a defined window: how many retained/shared dispatches occurred, how many fan-outs had conflicts, which paths repeated, and which conflict kinds; the `yaah-6xyl.4` revisit criteria can be evaluated without reading individual proposals.

title: feat(proposal): short proposal-id aliases; document per-boot suffix reset
description:
Source: usage-report addendum §5.

Proposal ids are `proposal:<UnixNano>:<seq>`; the `:N` suffix resets per process boot (uniqueness comes from the timestamp). They are unwieldy to retype.

## Ask

Accept a short unambiguous suffix (`:7`) in the `proposal` tool when it resolves uniquely, and document the per-boot suffix reset. Reject ambiguous or unknown short ids loudly.

## Acceptance

- `show`/`settle`/`continue`/`fork` accept a unique short suffix.
- Ambiguous or unknown ids fail loudly with the candidates (for ambiguity).
- Docs state the id shape and that the suffix is per-boot.

title: pubsub: spike — external event library behind the Broker/View seam (Watermill) if durability is ever needed
description:
Do not adopt an external event library (Watermill, kelindar/event, townbell/bus, etc.) for the in-process agent loop: the sealed events.Event interface + exhaustive_test + sequential HandleEvent guarantee + drop-vs-must-deliver semantics are better served by the ~150-line internal broker, and external libs (string topics, handler-error/ack semantics, marshaling, goroutine-per-subscriber) would need a translation adapter anyway.

Only revisit if a concrete need appears: durable event replay / events surviving restart / external or plugin consumers subscribing. In that case spike Watermill (GoChannel first, then its SQLite pub/sub) behind the existing Broker/View seam, keeping events.Event as the contract. Record the trigger conditions here so the decision is not re-litigated without new requirements.

title: acp: implement authenticate and advertise authMethods
description: internal/acp/server.go:416-418 always rejects the authenticate method ('authenticate is not offered'), and internal/acp/protocol.go:88-91 defines AuthMethod as a placeholder struct that is never populated - authMethods is always an empty array in the initialize response.  An empty authMethods array is the spec-correct way to say 'no auth required', so this is not broken. It only becomes a gap when a client is configured to authenticate.  Decide and implement: - if yaah stays unauthenticated, drop the dead AuthMethod type and the authenticate branch so the surface is honest - if yaah gains auth, implement the authenticate method and populate authMethods in the initialize response  Whichever way this goes, the answer must be documented in docs/acp.md and reflected in the initialize response.

title: acp: support image and audio content blocks in session/prompt
description: internal/acp/server.go:621-625 renders image and audio ContentBlocks as the literal strings '[image content not supported by this agent]' and '[audio content not supported by this agent]'. renderPrompt (server.go) flattens ContentBlocks to plain text, so multimodal prompts are accepted but their payload is thrown away.  Scope the work: - decide which modalities yaah's providers actually support and implement those - the ACP content block -> yaah message content mapping (image -> the provider's image part, audio -> the provider's audio part, resource/resource_link -> the referenced file contents) - reject unsupported modalities with a clear error rather than substituting a placeholder string, so a caller can tell the difference between 'no image in the prompt' and 'image dropped'  Check internal/types for the provider-agnostic message content representation before adding a second path.

title: acp: split internal/acp/server.go (638 LOC, over the repo's file-size guidance)
description: internal/acp/server.go is 638 lines. docs/code-organization.md:53-60 sets the guidance at 500-800 lines per file, at which point the file should be split by responsibility. server.go currently holds: the Server struct and Session interface, the JSON-RPC connection writer, the Run loop and signal handling, method dispatch, handleSessionNew, handlePrompt, handleCancel, stopRun, renderPrompt and the question handler.  Split along the existing seams - the file already has natural boundaries: - protocol/connection plumbing (connection writer, rawOf, send helpers) - dispatch (the method table and routing) - session lifecycle (handleSessionNew, session/load, session/cancel, stopRun) - prompt handling (handlePrompt, renderPrompt, the held-open turn)  Keep this a pure move: no behaviour change, and the existing server_test.go must pass unchanged.

title: consolidate: P2 guardrails (schema validation, description limits, security scan, recursion guard)
description: P2 of docs/compaction-as-sleep.md §8. Port hermes safety stack: frontmatter validation, description-length limit, security scan, archive-not-delete, provenance stamp, recursion guard. Required before enabling unattended writes.

title: memory: P3 multi-level memory + light/deep sleep
description: P3 of docs/compaction-as-sleep.md §8. Short/medium/long memory tiers (directions 4/5); cheap 'light sleep' vs expensive 'deep sleep' staging; tie the consolidation product into the tiers.

description: P4 of docs/compaction-as-sleep.md §8 (optional, low priority). memory stats / journey-style view; hermes's learning graph is a render, not a store.

title: docs: ACP credential/auth-method story (authMethods, authenticate, provider env vars)
description:
Registration forces yaah to stop being SILENT about how it authenticates. Document the credential story that the registry entry will advertise.

Cover:
- The authMethods yaah declares (from yaah-aon) and what each one means to a client that supports ACP auth.
- Provider credential env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ...) and precedence vs providers.json.
- What 'authenticate' does and does not validate (no network call on declaration).
- Explicitly state that the agent's security posture (session/request_permission approval bridge, tool-kind classification, sandbox/egress layers) is NOT surfaced through ACP and is configured yaah-side.

This overlaps yaah-yq1 (rewrite ACP docs: acp_cmd.go help, docs/features.md, README.md, dev-loop SKILL.md handshake example). Coordinate rather than duplicate — this bead owns the auth/credential section specifically.

title: ACP: auth.logout + terminal-typed auth bridging yaah login; promote embeddedContext and mcpCapabilities
description: Multiple small capability gaps: (1) no logout method / agentCapabilities.auth.logout though yaah has yaah login/logout (OAuth device flow); (2) no type:'terminal' auth method (clientCapabilities.auth.terminal - Zed does this for Gemini via spawn-*-cli), which would give Zed real login UX instead of the current name-check-only authenticate (auth.go:46-56 validates the declared id, never credentials - keep that contract, but a terminal method can launch yaah login); (3) promptCapabilities.embeddedContext unpromoted though renderPrompt already handles resource blocks as embedded text (server.go:1408-1447) - image/audio stay honestly false; (4) mcpCapabilities.http/.sse unpromoted (session/new mcpServers forwards stdio only). Keep the static auth catalog config-independent (registry probes on cold HOME, auth.go:1-16). Acceptance: Zed can trigger yaah login from the auth picker; embedded resource blocks are accepted in prompts; HTTP/SSE MCP manifests are either supported or still silently stdio-only per docs.

title: ACP wire fidelity: wrong error code for unwired list/delete, JSON-RPC batches crash-parse, toolKind table drift
description: Three fidelity nits: (1) session/list and session/delete return -32601 'method not found' when their callback is unwired (server.go:626-629, 797-803) - the METHOD exists; use a clearer code/message so clients do not infer the method is unknown; (2) JSON-RPC batch arrays (a [...] line) fail to unmarshal into Message and yield -32700 with id:null (server.go:1007-1012) - either support batches or return -32600 with a clear message; (3) the toolKind name table (approval.go:38-63) drifts: patch/replace land in 'other' while edit is KindEdit, todowrite/plan map to KindThink though they write - derive the kind from the tool registry instead of a hardcoded list. Acceptance: tests pin each behaviour; kind mapping matches tool semantics.

title: ACP v2 tracking: draft spec removes fs/*, terminal/*, session/set_mode, session/load, tool_call
description: Tracking note for the v2-targeted children: ACP v2 (draft; Zed dual-stack behind flag) REMOVES fs/*, terminal/*, session/set_mode, session/load, tool_call — the v1 work (fs/*.10, terminal/*.14, mode modeling /*.8) needs a v2 note (v2 roadmap: implement fs/terminal via new surfaces or document as v1-only). Also note: v1-added diff content blocks/locations/v elicitation/usage cost are all removed or reshaped in v2; keep yaah's v2 tracking here.

title: ACP: client-side terminal integration for shell tool calls (live output in Zed)
description: Shell-tool support so commands run in a visible Zed terminal pane with live output instead of opaque rawOutput strings. Implement the agent->client terminal methods per the spec's terminals page (agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/terminals): create (returns terminalId immediately), output (a REQUEST, not a notification, with truncation + exitStatus), wait_for_exit, the non-releasing interruption variant, and release (the spec requires the agent to always pair every create with a release). Gated on clientCapabilities.terminal (parsed but unused today, protocol.go:56-58). Tool-call content can also carry a {terminalId} block. Acceptance: shell tool calls surface in a Zed terminal when the cap is advertised; output polling respects outputByteLimit; every terminal handle is cleaned up on completion AND when a turn ends early. NOTE: the shell guard blocks certain spec vocabulary in command lines, which is why this description rides in a file; the exact method names are on the spec page cited above.

title: spike: child-process MCP server for webfetch/http under the jail
description: webfetch and http are the only built-in tools doing network I/O in yaah's own goroutine, outside any confinement (tools.go:291-305 hostNetworkLeafTools; omitted under restrictive egress at runner.go:1262,1736). They are also the cleanest extraction candidates (stdlib + prompts only, no Workspace/PathValidator setters). Spike shipping them as a small child-process MCP server so the existing jail governs them. Open questions: DangerClassifier loss (MCP tools cannot implement it - wiring_mcp.go:15-19) and name-keyed policy tables (hostNetworkLeafTools, goToolchainTools). This is the only recommended tool externalization.

title: refactor: re-point view consumers at internal/agent/events
description: Events live in leaf internal/agent/events (imports only internal/types) and are re-exported via internal/agent/event_aliases.go:9. TUI (internal/tui/proxy.go:11), ACP (internal/acp/view.go:8) and the web/REPL views therefore compile-link the whole engine (memory pulls sqlite, providers pulls the Anthropic SDK) just to spell agent.Event/agent.View. Move the View seam into internal/agent/events and alias it in internal/agent; update the 4 consumers. Caution: events/exhaustive_test.go locates consumers by relative source paths - update those literals in the same change.

title: chore: delete dead skipMCP/skipOtel params on newAgentSessionWithOptions
description: wiring.go:136 takes (opts, skipMCP, skipOtel). Every production caller passes false,false (wiring.go:41, root_cmd.go:89, serve.go:116, acp_cmd.go:115); only resume_picker_test.go:317 passes true,true. The documented rationale (wiring.go:133-135, tview input sluggish on Windows) is unreachable because tui.go:58 goes through newAgentSession(). Delete the two params or fold them into SessionOptions so the flag seam stays singular.

title: chore: mark internal/sandboxfake as test-only
description: internal/sandboxfake is 45KB (3 prod files) but imported ONLY by internal/tools/workspace_*_test.go - it is never linked into the binary yet counts as the second-largest platform package. Rename to sandboxtest (or equivalent test-only naming) so production-surface counts stop including it. Optional follow-up: group internal/{jail,gitsandbox,sandboxfake} under internal/sandbox/ to make the layer legible.

title: json_query write/delete silently reformats the whole file and ignores MarshalIndent errors
description: internal/tools/json_query.go (doWrite/doDelete): the file is round-tripped through any and rewritten with json.MarshalIndent, whose error is discarded. A one-key write sorts every object key alphabetically, normalises numbers and rewrites indentation across the whole document while reporting only "Set X to Y". On a large package.json this produces a diff the user did not ask for and the model does not know it caused. setJSONPath comment says "create containers as needed" but a missing intermediate key returns "key not found".

title: ls.md advertises human-readable sizes the tool never prints; ignored-only dirs reported empty
description: internal/prompts/tools/ls.md claims "Shows files and subdirectories with human-readable sizes" but ls.go listDir never calls Size(). Separately, ls silently hides every commonIgnoreDirs entry, so a directory containing only vendor/ reports "(empty directory)".

title: edit: fuzzy-match verification check is tautological (its comment promises a guarantee it cannot give)
description: internal/tools/edit.go (executeSingleEdit): the comment says the mapped-back fuzzy match is verified against original content "to prevent silent corruption when fuzzy match maps to wrong location", but matched is by construction a substring of content, so strings.Count >= 1 always and the check can only detect duplicated text, never a wrong location — the exact risk the comment names.

title: bisect: checkFound regex can never match git bisect log output (permanently no-op safety net)
description: internal/tools/bisect.go: bisectFoundRe matches "<sha> is the first bad commit", but checkFound runs git bisect log which renders "# first bad commit: [abc1234] subject". The regex can never match, so the discovery path checkFound was written to cover is silently never covered.

title: go_mod dry_run for add/remove/upgrade is a canned message, not a preview
description: internal/tools/go_mod.go (~:241-284): only tidy performs a real preview (go mod tidy -diff). For add/remove/upgrade dry_run fabricates "would run: go get X@latest", drops params.Flags from the message and forces success:true, so an unresolvable/typo/private module all preview as success. go_mod.md sells dry_run as "preview destructive operations without modifying go.mod".

title: go_refactor info: empty-package fallback is dead code; empty dirs look like a successful load
description: internal/tools/go_refactor.go (~:126-159): the header "Package: %s (%d packages loaded)" is written before the loops so the out.Len()==0 fallback can never fire. The genuine empty case (packages.Load returns zero packages because dir holds no Go files) returns a header claiming "(0 packages loaded)" with no explanation nothing was analysed.

title: go_refactor.md overstates the tool (no cross-package refactoring exists)
description: internal/prompts/tools/go_refactor.md claims "Operates at the AST level so cross-package references are handled correctly", but the tool is imports.Process (goimports, single file) plus a read-only symbol listing — there is no cross-package rewriting anywhere. A model reaching for go_refactor to rename a symbol across packages gets a silent no-op class of "already formatted" success. The doc also omits that info takes dir and silently defaults it to ".".

title: background_process.md says list shows "all running processes" but it lists every tracked process including corpses
description: internal/prompts/tools/background_process.md: "action list shows all running processes", but background_process.go (~:77-88) prints every entry the manager ever created (running/finished/stopped/error) and nothing is evicted. After a few restart cycles the "running" view is mostly corpses and the model reads stale state as live infrastructure.

title: todowrite model-facing contract oversells a list it cannot address by identity
description: internal/tools/todo.go: item IDs are positional (td-%d) and the schema has no id field, so inserting/reordering silently re-keys every later item and there is no way to reference/update a single item (every call is whole-list replacement). todo.md "Creates and manages a structured todo list" invites per-item edits the schema cannot express. Contract/docs complaint, distinct from the closed yaah-2z5 backend idea.

title: memory_search silently degrades vector to FTS and discards the vector error; retrieval path unlabelled
description: internal/tools/memory.go: three distinct states (embedding server absent, embedding server errored, vectors returned nothing) collapse into one unlabelled FTS result set because err is discarded and nothing names the path used — compare the sibling tool in the same file which labels hits [semantic]. A model cannot tell whether an empty recall means "not known" or "semantic path was down".

title: skill search has no relevance floor — with an embedder every skill is reported as a match
description: internal/tools/skill.go (skillSearch/formatSearchResults): every discovered skill enters matches regardless of score, so "Found N matching skill(s)" is just the skill count and the tool never reports a miss (unlike the keyword path which says "No skills matched"). An agent asking for a capability that does not exist gets ten skills scored 0.00-0.1 presented as matches. Per-skill embedding errors are swallowed (embeddings[i], _ = emb.Embed) and silently score zero.

title: memory_update ownership guard is conditional on Scope while memory_promote is unconditional — write path is less protected
description: internal/tools/memory.go: MemoryUpdateTool applies its SessionID ownership check only when t.Scope != "" (wiring sets Scope only for the consolidator), so an ordinary session memory_update can rewrite another session atom or a global fact by id, whereas the lower-risk MemoryPromoteTool refuses atoms outside the caller session whenever SessionID is set. The asymmetry is undocumented and reads as oversight.

title: subagent_jobs cancel masks a reaped or finished job as a successful cancel
description: internal/tools/subagent_jobs.go (~:157-163): Cancel returning true only proves the id was known; Status is re-queried with its ok flag dropped, so a reaped job yields a zero-value snapshot force-labelled "cancelled" and marshalled as a successful cancellation of a job that no longer exists. Cancelling an already-finished job reports the stale snapshot as the outcome, and "already done" vs "never existed" are indistinguishable.

title: delegate timeout_seconds is a dead knob — parsed and clamped but declared in neither schema
description: internal/tools/delegate.go:141 parses timeout_seconds and clampTimeoutSeconds exists, but neither Schema() branch (delegate_schema.go static :17-30 or dynamic :100-135) declares the field, so a strict-schema provider can never send it and the parse/clamp/ResolveTimeout paths are reachable only from tests. delegate.md meanwhile says "Timeouts are configured per role", contradicting the per-call override.

title: list_subagents.md advertises a "default model" field and a hardcoded role roster the tool never emits
description: internal/prompts/tools/list_subagents.md promises "name, description, default model, and available tools" and enumerates built-in role names, but SubAgentInfo has no model field and the renderer prints Role ID/Contract/Description/Tools/Budget only. The enumerated roster also goes stale the moment a user adds a role — the tool exists for runtime-discovered roles.

title: retained report-lane teardown failures are logged, never surfaced — leaked worktree invisible to the orchestrator
description: internal/tools/retained.go (~:230-243): report-lane teardown failures only slog.Warn (worktree discard failed / scope missing) and the function returns the result unchanged, unlike the proposal lane which folds provErr/sealErr into env.Error. The one lane with no record to recover from is the one that stays quiet.

title: webfetch discards the response body on HTTP >= 400 (error masking)
description: internal/tools/webfetch.go (~:93-95) returns a bare "webfetch: HTTP %d" for status >= 400 and throws away the body, while the sibling http tool returns it. A 403/404 page usually explains itself (auth message, missing route list, API error JSON); the model cannot distinguish wrong-URL from WAF-blocked and typically retries the same URL.

title: webfetch: "markdown" and "text" formats are the same code path — the markdown conversion the doc promises does not exist
description: internal/tools/webfetch.go (~:109-121): both "text" and the default (documented as markdown) call htmlToText, which only strips tags/scripts/styles and decodes five entities — no headings, links or code fences survive, and every href is gone. webfetch.md sells three formats where two are byte-identical and the third ("markdown") discards structure the tool claims to preserve.

title: webfetch format html bypasses the tool 8KiB output cap (up to 2MiB into the loop, no truncation marker)
description: internal/tools/webfetch.go (~:101-103): the html branch returns string(body) raw while every other branch applies toolResultMaxLen (8192) with a truncation marker. One call can hand up to 2MiB (io.LimitReader 2MiB) to the loop, betting on the downstream loop-level truncateToolResult instead.

title: http tool prints the status code twice (HTTP 200 200 OK)
description: internal/tools/http.go:200 formats "HTTP %d %s" with resp.StatusCode and resp.Status, but resp.Status already contains the code ("200 OK"), so every result opens with "HTTP 200 200 OK" — the first line the model reads looks like a mangled response.

title: no test enforces doc/tool parity — description test covers 11 of 40 embedded docs
description: internal/tools/registry_test.go:114-127 checks Description non-empty for a hand-written slice of 11 tools while schemas_test.go checks every registered tool. Nothing reads prompts.ToolsFS or asserts that every tools/*.md is consumed and matches the schema/Execute surface, so every doc-based claim drifts silently (read.md bytes, patch.md file path, git.md fetch, webfetch.md markdown, memory_search.md tag were all found by this audit) and new tools get a schema check but no description check.

title: document the isolation vs egress matrix in one place ("isolated" does not mean "no network")
description: Confinement is asserted on two independent axes: workspace isolation in internal/tools (NewIsolatedRegistry filters isHostOnlyTool; registry_isolated_test.go pins the delta is exactly [go_refactor]) and egress in internal/agent/runner (restrictiveEgress + hostNetworkLeafTools = {http,webfetch}). A workspace-isolated-but-not-confined session keeps full in-process egress through http/webfetch, so any doc or audit claiming "isolated sessions cannot reach the network" is wrong. The matrix exists only as code in two packages.

title: compaction model routing: do not summarize a session with the same weak model that runs it, by default
description: Incident factor (yaah-v378): no compaction provider/model is configured, so compactModel falls back to cm.Model — here mimo-v2.6-pro, the model that echoed the summary template with '(none)' in all ten sections. Decide and implement the default: route compaction to agent.small_model when set (mimo-v2.6-flash here), document the compaction provider/model knobs next to the existing compaction tuning block in config.yaml, and emit a startup warning when the compaction model equals the main model. AC: with small_model set, compaction uses it (assert in a wiring test); the config docs name the knobs; the warning fires on the degenerate config.

title: decide: retain top-level session runs (whole-run parity)
description:
# Decide whether top-level session runs become retained

## Context

Shepherd can retain a top-level run, so the whole session — not just child
tasks — is reversible. yaah deliberately leaves the orchestrator unconfined on
the host: it has ambient access, mutates the working tree directly, and cannot
produce a proposal. That split is load-bearing for interactive UX and the
terminal-bench contract, but it is currently an undocumented divergence rather
than a decision with a scope.

## Options

1. **Keep it.** Host orchestrator stays unconfined and unretained. Interactive
   responsiveness and the benchmark contract stay as-is; the gap report marks
   this intentional, not a gap.
2. **Opt-in retained root.** A session flag forks the root into a worktree and
   settles at exit. Cost: TUI/web file access, checkpoints, and recovery all
   need the root to be a scope; settlement becomes a user-facing step.
3. **Hybrid.** Retain only for non-interactive/one-shot runs, keep interactive
   sessions unconfined.

## Acceptance

- The decision is recorded with rationale and consequences for checkpoints,
  recovery, TUI/web, and terminal-bench.
- If "retain": follow-up beads filed for root scope creation, settlement UX, and
  recovery, with a default that does not change silently.
- If "keep": the parity scorecard marks whole-run retention as declined, and
  `docs/configuration.md` explains the split.

title: docs: parity ledger — refresh the Shepherd gap report and pin it with a drift guard

title: ACP: diff content on tool_call for edit/move tools
description:
Render file modifications as client-side diff viewers by emitting ACP diff
content on tool_call / tool_call_update for edit- and move-class tools.

## Surface

- Tool-call content blocks of `{"type":"diff", ...}` allOf-merged with the
- Diff definition (path, oldText, newText, ...; v1 schema def Diff).
- yaah's own protocol notes already flag this: internal/acp/protocol.go:432
  ("diff" and "terminal" exist in the schema but are not produced by yaah
  yet) and UpdateContent currently wraps only standard content blocks.

## Mapping

- The edit tool (and move, when content is textual) attaches Diff content to
  its tool_call_update; the text summary in toolfmt stays as a fallback for
  clients that do not render diffs (content negotiation: review whether any
  clientCapabilities gate exists; if not, send both diff block and summary).
- Keep tool result text (what the model sees) untouched — this is purely the
  client-facing update payload.

## Acceptance

An edit tool call renders as a diff widget in a capable client instead of a
text blob; tests pin the block shape against the schema; docs/acp.md notes
the richer tool_call content.

Priority P3: pure presentation, no behavior change. Rides along with any
tool-surface work.

title: ACP: remaining client widgets (umbrella) — terminal, state/subagent, notice, compaction, plan_update, providers, auth

title: docs(code): world fact shape diverges from the parity ledger
description:
# World fact shape diverges from the parity ledger

## Context

`docs/shepherd-parity.md` (Observation) documents the per-dispatch fact as:

`yaah.subagent.world.v1 { requested, resolved, backend, reason, enforced }`

`recordWorldFact` (`internal/tools/retained.go`) emits:

`{ requested, resolved, degraded, reason }`

So two promised fields are missing (`backend`, `enforced`) and one real field is
undocumented (`degraded`). A trace consumer written against the ledger cannot
tell which boundary enforced a container world, which matters while the
container lane is the one non-jail world.

## Acceptance

- Code and ledger agree on one shape; either emit `backend` and `enforced`
  (derived from the resolved world) or correct the ledger and explain why not.
- A `world` fact test asserts the key set, so the drift guard catches the next
  change.
- `docs/shepherd-parity.md` and any `yaah.subagent.world.v1` references match.

title: bug(doctor): dispatch-world preflight ignores per-role world overrides
description:
# Dispatch-world preflight ignores per-role world overrides

## Context

`CheckDispatchWorld` (`internal/doctor/checks.go`) resolves the ladder from the
session-level config only. Its own comment records the limitation: "Role
overrides are not resolved here (doctor reports the session default)."

A role configured with `world: container` on a host that cannot provide one
therefore reports healthy in `yaah doctor`, then fails closed at dispatch. The
same blind spot applies to per-role `grants`: the preflight uses
`len(sc.Grants) > 0` and cannot see a role-level restrictive set, so a role that
will refuse an advisory placement is not flagged.

## Acceptance

  explicit WARN naming the roles it did not check).

description:
# Lower world-relative grants onto container dispatch worlds

## Context

`agents.subagent.grants` is implemented for worktree worlds: RW roots become
`ConfinementSpec.WritableRoots`, RO roots are omitted so writes are denied, and
an advisory placement refuses a restrictive set (D10).

A container world refuses the same set:
`containerRefusal` returns "per-binding grants are not lowered onto container
worlds yet". With `world: auto`, any restrictive grant set forces report
dispatches back to the worktree; with `world: container` it fails closed. So
authority and the container lane cannot be combined today.

The container boundary is whole-container, not whole-world: the sandbox root is
`workspace.root` (`/workspace`), and grants are world-relative. Lowering them
means shaping what the container can mount or write under its workdir, not
reusing the Landlock writable-root rule.

## Acceptance

- Decide and record whether container worlds lower grants (mounts/roots/bind
  policy) or continue to refuse them.
- If lowering: RW/RO semantics match the worktree lane (RO writes denied, RW
  disjoint roots, unknown/escaping paths refused) and are tested.
- If refusing: state the limitation in D10/the ledger and make the resolver's
  degradation message name grants as the reason (it already does).
- `world: auto` + grants has one documented behavior, not an incidental one.

title: Investigate consolidating state.db and trace.db content
description:
# Investigate consolidating state.db and trace.db content

## Context

`yaah-o86` made `trace.db` a content-bearing transcript mirror: session
context, assistant content/reasoning/signature, tool calls, and tool output
bodies now duplicate much of the orchestrator's text in `state.db`. The
overlap is intentional for crash-safe evidence and sub-agent recovery, but it
is currently unmeasured and unmanaged.

Observed overlaps:
- `sessions.system_prompt` / `cwd` / `model` and the trace `session:context` fact
- user messages and `turn:created` prompts
- assistant messages (content, reasoning, signature, tool calls) and
  `assistant:message` facts
- tool result messages and `tool:<name>:result` captures
- tool-call arguments in `messages.tool_calls` and trace declarations

Not redundant:
- sub-agent intermediate messages exist only in trace (`state.db` skips them)
- causal graph, scope/frontier, witness and retained-context facts exist only
  in trace
- FTS5, embeddings, pagination, titles, session picker and compaction state
  exist only in state.db
- trace caps free text at 64KiB and marks truncation/spill; it is not a
  byte-exact backup
- compaction deletes state rows while trace retains the prior facts
- `DeleteSession` removes state rows and `trace_owners` mappings but cannot
  delete trace facts (the kernel exposes no owner-deletion API)

## Decision needed

Decide whether to keep the two-tier model, deduplicate bodies, co-locate the
stores, or make one a projection. No code change is implied by this bead; the
deliverable is a measured decision.

## Questions

1. How many bytes are actually duplicated for representative main sessions?
   Measure `state.db` message/session text vs trace content payloads, including
   the 64KiB cap and spill-ref cases.
2. Does trace content need to be byte-exact? If not, the current caps are fine;
   if it is a recovery source, define what is intentionally lossy.
3. What is the retention contract? Should session deletion redact trace facts,
   and what kernel API is needed to do it without leaving orphan contexts,
   frontiers or witnesses?
4. Is a shared content-addressed body store better than co-location? Both
   preserve FTS/vector retrieval in state.db and keep fact digests meaningful.
5. What does the kernel need to expose (`TraceStore` interface, owner delete,
   retrieval hooks) before co-location is viable? Relates to upstream
   `shepherd-runtime-go-s3u` and the storage delta report (4.1–4.5).

## Acceptance

- Written decision with measured bytes for at least one long main session and
  one sub-agent-heavy session.
- Explicit retention/deletion semantics, including what `yaah sessions delete`
  does and does not remove today.
- Ranked options with migration/rollback and kernel-dependency notes.
- If consolidation is chosen, a follow-up implementation plan; if not, the
  two-tier contract is recorded as the decision and linked from docs/storage.md.

## Non-goals

- Replacing `state.db` with trace facts while the kernel lacks FTS/vector and
  read-side pagination.
- Deleting `trace_owners` rows or raw-SQLing kernel tables as a shortcut.
- Changing `state.db` compaction semantics in this investigation.

title: spike: decide dispatch retry/fallback/recover policy and combinator parity
description:
# Decision: retry / fallback / recover for delegate dispatch

Reference: `shepherd_runtime.combinators.retry` (`retry`, `fallback`,
`recover`) and `shepherd_runtime.combinators.gating` (`gate`, `budget`,
`timeout`).

## Reference semantics

- `retry` runs a task in a fresh fork up to N attempts, discards failed forks,
  supports a result predicate (`until`), delay/backoff, and merges the last
  attempt anyway when `until` still fails.
- `fallback` tries a sequence of tasks; first success wins; failed forks are
  discarded.
- `recover` runs once; on error it discards the fork and returns a handler
  supplied default value.
- The useful invariant is: a failed attempt leaves no retained effects.

## Recommended yaah design (to validate in this spike)

Put retry at the **dispatch boundary**, not inside the streaming agent loop.
Every attempt gets a fresh proposal/scope ID, trace owner, worktree/container
world, timeout, and usage accounting.

Lane-aware retry matrix:

| Lane / phase | Policy |
|---|---|
| Preflight failure (daemon, image, bootstrap, provisioning) | Retry with backoff; nothing ran |
| Report lane (worktree or container) | Retry on timeout/provider/transient failure; world is destroyed |
| Proposal lane before seal | Retry only if provisioning failed before any work |
| Proposal lane after seal | No automatic retry: a sealed partial is reviewable and consume-once |
| Shared lane | No automatic retry: it mutates the host directly |
| Parent cancellation / user halt | Never retry |

Failure classes: `preflight_transient`, `provider_transient`, `timeout`,
`stuck`, `content`, `configuration`, `cancelled`, `sealed`. Only the first four
are candidates for retry; configuration/cancel/sealed never retry.

Budget semantics: `timeout_seconds` is the TOTAL dispatch budget, each attempt
gets the remaining budget, `max_iterations`/`max_turns` are per attempt, usage
is aggregated, and `max_elapsed_seconds` bounds backoff.

Evidence: per-attempt `yaah.subagent.dispatch_attempt.v1` fact (attempt,
status, retryable, failure_class, scope_id, trace_owner_id, proposal_id); final
envelope gains `attempts`, `retried`, and attempt IDs.

## Dispositions

- **Adopt:** scoped retry for preflight + report lanes; config
  `agents.subagent.retry` with per-role override; total-timeout semantics;
  attempt trace evidence.
- **Decline for v1:** generic `fallback` over roles/prompts/models (different
  lanes/tool belts/output contracts; orchestrator can choose explicitly) and
  generic `recover`/default values (can look like success; structured failure
  envelopes already exist).
- **Defer:** auto-retry of sealed proposals; fallback/recover policy. File
  decisions after v1 evidence.
- **No arbitrary `until` predicates:** use deterministic built-in quality
  checks, coordinated with `yaah-hxk3.1`; do not add a predicate DSL.
- **Decline the authoring API:** `task`/`step`/`sequence`/`branch`/`loop` and
  effect-stream combinators remain Python-SDK-specific; the LLM orchestrator
  handles composition.
- **Coordinate:** `yaah-95ri` (parallel/speculation efficiency) and
  `yaah-9bq` (overlap visibility); do not duplicate their work.

## Deliverable

A short decision document with the final adopt/decline table, lane rules,
budget semantics, config/API shape, and follow-up beads. No runtime
implementation in this spike.

title: Batching compliance: 1.26 tool calls per assistant turn despite the cardinal rule (46 steps vs Hermes 34)
description:
## Terms (as used in this bead)

- **step** — one assistant turn, i.e. one model API call. The extractor counts
  assistant messages; a step may carry several tool calls.
- **batching** — emitting multiple independent tool calls in a *single*
  assistant turn rather than one call per turn. yaah's `identity.md` opens with
  a section titled "## Cardinal rule: batch tool calls" and states the cost
  explicitly: "Five 1-read turns cost 5× the time and context of one 5-read
  turn."
- **calls per message** — total tool calls divided by assistant messages, the
  direct measure of batching adherence. 1.0 means every turn made exactly one
  call and the cardinal rule had no effect.

## Finding

Measured across all five tasks of the 2026-10-29 run
(`bench/terminal-bench/RESULTS.md`): 58 tool calls over 46 assistant messages
= **1.26 calls per message**. The distribution is
`{1 call: 30 messages, 2: 8, 4: 3}` — **65% of turns made a single call**
despite the cardinal rule being the first thing in the system prompt.

The same five tasks cost Hermes 0.19.0 **34 steps** and OpenCode **40**, against
yaah's 46. Each extra step re-sends the whole per-call floor (~10.5K tokens
after the 2026-10-31 gates, ~13.4K before) and adds a turn of latency: yaah's
wall time was 184s against OpenCode's 134s on identical tasks and an identical
score.

## Why this was deferred rather than implemented

This is **model adherence, not harness structure** — there is no obviously
wrong code to fix. yaah already states the rule, states it first, and states
the cost of violating it; deepseek-flash largely ignores it anyway. The
candidate levers each carry real regression risk and none is validated:

- stronger or repeated prompt emphasis costs floor tokens on every call to fix
  a per-turn behaviour, and the floor is the thing the sibling beads are trying
  to shrink — the two pull against each other
- mechanically merging adjacent single-call turns changes tool-approval and
  trace semantics, and yaah's trace/settlement guarantees are the product
- a different model may simply batch better, which would make this a
  model-selection note rather than a yaah defect

Whether the gap is yaah's prompt or this model tier's tool-calling behaviour
cannot be settled from one trial of one model.

## Acceptance criteria

- A second model tier is measured on the same five tasks before any yaah-side
  change is made, to separate "yaah's prompt does not induce batching" from
  "deepseek-flash does not batch". If a second tier batches well on the
  unchanged prompt, close this as a model-tier note.
- If yaah-side work is justified, it is A/B'd at **3+ trials per task** on both
  the coding suite and `bench/orchestration-tasks`, and rejected if
  resolved-count or trace compliance drops.
- Any prompt-side change reports its own floor cost, so the batching gain is
  not paid for with a per-call regression that exceeds it.

## Expected benefit

Mainly **wall-clock latency**, not spend. The extra steps re-send a floor that
is 95-98% cache reads at $0.003/M, so the dollar cost of yaah's 46-vs-34 step
gap is small; the 184s-vs-134s wall-time gap is the user-visible part. Closing
it to Hermes's 34 steps would also cut roughly 12 × floor tokens of prompt
volume, which matters for context-window headroom on long tasks.

title: feat(dispatch): safe retry for preflight and report dispatches
description:
# Safe dispatch retry — v1

Implements the scoped retry policy from `yaah-hxk3.5`, after that decision is
accepted. This is not a port of Python's generic `retry()` combinator.

## Scope

- Retry at the dispatch boundary so every attempt gets a fresh proposal/scope
  ID, trace owner, world, timeout, and usage accounting.
- Add `agents.subagent.retry` with per-role override:
  - `max_attempts`
  - `on` / retry classes
  - `delay_seconds`, `backoff`, `max_elapsed_seconds`
- Only retry:
  - preflight-transient failures (daemon/image/bootstrap/provisioning),
  - report-lane timeout/stuck/provider-transient failures.
- Never retry:
  - a sealed proposal (after-seal),
  - the shared lane (host mutation),
  - parent cancellation / user halt,
  - configuration errors.
- Proposal lane: retry only provisioning failures before any work; never
  re-run after a proposal is registered.
- `timeout_seconds` is the total dispatch budget; each attempt gets the
  remaining budget. `max_iterations`/`max_turns` remain per attempt. Aggregate
  usage across attempts.
- Record `yaah.subagent.dispatch_attempt.v1` per attempt (attempt, status,
  retryable, failure_class, scope_id, trace_owner_id, proposal_id).
- Extend the delegate envelope with `attempts`, `retried`, and attempt IDs.
- Background dispatches inherit the same policy through the job runner.

## Out of scope

- Generic `fallback`, generic `recover`, arbitrary `until` predicates.
- Auto-retry of sealed proposals (future decision).
- New authoring/combinator API.

## Acceptance

Tests cover: success on attempt 2; retryable preflight/report failure;
non-retryable sealed proposal/shared/cancel/configuration; total timeout split
across attempts; backoff/max-elapsed; attempt facts and envelope fields;
background dispatch; no duplicate proposals and no leaked worktrees/containers.
Docs/config reference and no silent behavior change when retry is unset.

title: fix(conflict): make execution-time tracking evidence-based
description:
# Phase 2: evidence-based execution-time conflict tracking

Replace the current path-touch heuristic in `ConflictTracker` with evidence
that a write actually happened and can conflict.

Current limitations:
- records before execution, so failed writes count;
- only structured write/edit/delete tools, not shell/script/generated writes;
- raw paths, no workspace-relative normalization;
- isolated-world path touches are reported like real clobbers;
- per-parent-batch reset does not line up with background/cross-turn work.

## Scope

- Record after successful execution; ignore failed/no-op writes.
- Normalize to workspace-relative slash paths and handle case sensitivity
  explicitly.
- Capture before/after content digest and mode where the backend can provide it.
- Distinguish:
  - shared-lane actual write conflicts;
  - retained-world speculative overlap (proposal manifests are authoritative);
  - unknown mutations from shell/scripts (do not claim more than observed).
- Align background/cross-turn records with the proposal IDs or dispatch labels
  they belong to.
- Keep the existing `CONFLICT:` user message as a view over the typed records;
  do not let prose be the only channel.
- Record conflict facts with enough identity for `proposal list`/`show`.

## Acceptance

Tests cover failed writes not counted, successful same-path divergent writes,
same-path identical writes, normalized path variants, shell-induced changes
marked unknown rather than falsely conflict-free, retained-world warnings
labeled speculative, background dispatch, and shared-lane clobber detection.

title: feat(proposal): conflict resolution workflow without auto-merge
description:
# Phase 3: conflict resolution workflow without auto-merge

Give the orchestrator enough information to resolve conflicts deliberately.
Path-disjoint apply remains the default; no automatic content synthesis.

## Scope

- Extend `proposal show` / list conflict entries with a base/current/proposed
  view for each divergent path (or a reference to an artifact containing it).
- Make it explicit that `apply` is path-disjoint and will refuse divergent
  overlaps.
- Support the existing safe endings:
  - discard one proposal;
  - release one for manual review;
  - create a new coordinated proposal after editing.
- Optional, explicit `apply --strategy=three-way` for the worktree lane using
  Git merge machinery, fail-closed on textual conflicts; do not add a
  container-lane equivalent without a backend merge primitive.
- No new default settlement semantics; consume-once and basis checks remain.

## Acceptance

Tests cover: divergent same-path conflict display; identical duplicate is not
blocked; orchestrator can discard/release one side; optional worktree three-way
apply succeeds on non-overlapping hunks and fails closed on conflict; container
lane remains whole-path; no automatic merge; trace facts record the choice.

title: Add a native bead tool (create/update/show/search/list/close)
description:
Add a first-class `bead` tool so the agent can create/update/search this
repo's mandated issue tracker without composing multi-KB markdown through
shell here-strings.

## Motivation (observed 2026-11-02)

* AGENTS.md requires bd for all task tracking (no TodoWrite, no markdown TODO
  lists), so filing an issue is a routine agent operation, not an edge case.
  Today it costs 4-6 shell calls per issue and several thousand characters of
  quoting.
* Composing a 2-4 KB body inline is fragile: `bd create --body "..."` inside
  PowerShell needs here-strings, and `$` / backtick / quote handling varies by
  shell. The reliable path is write-file → `--body-file` → delete-file, i.e.
  three tools where one should exist.
* Verification is clumsy: `bd show <id> --json | ConvertFrom-Json` to confirm
  the body landed, because `bd show` prints long prose that must be re-read.
* The four issues filed from this session (search ignores, pruner stubs, write
  refusals, this tool) each took a separate write + create + verify cycle.

## Proposal

A native tool `bead` (registered wherever the belt is assembled, e.g.
`cmd/yaah/serve_tools.go` `registerServeTools` for stdio + HTTP MCP, and the
agent's tool set otherwise) with `action`-selected operations:

| action | required | optional |
|---|---|---|
| `create` | `title` | `type`, `priority`, `body`, `design`, `acceptance`, `labels`, `parent` |
| `update` | `id` | any of the above, plus `status`, `notes` |
| `show` | `id` | `json` |
| `search` | `query` | `status`, `limit` |
| `list` | — | `status`, `priority`, `labels`, `limit` |
| `close` | `id` | `reason` |

Requirements:

1. Long text goes in `body`/`design`/`acceptance` strings — no shell, no
   quoting. Internally write to a temp file under the workspace and pass
   `--body-file`/`--design-file`/`--acceptance` so the existing bd CLI
   contract is reused rather than reimplemented.
2. Return a compact JSON envelope (`{id, title, status, priority}`), not
   prose, so the caller can verify without a second call.
3. Fail with an actionable message when `bd` is absent from PATH
   (`exec.LookPath`) — the tool must not assume the CGO shim exists.
4. Speak to the CLI (`bd`) rather than opening the embedded Dolt DB
   directly: the DB is live and locked by concurrent agents, and the local
   `bd` version already handles schema/migration details.
5. Honour the conservative git policy: never commit, push, or `bd dolt push`
   from this tool.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bead create` with a 4 KB body round-trips exactly (test with a fixture
      body containing quotes, backticks, `$`, and CRLF).
- [ ] `bead show --json` returns the same structured envelope as `list`.
- [ ] Missing `bd` yields a clear one-line error, and the tool is skipped
      rather than crashing at startup.
- [ ] Tool appears in both stdio and HTTP MCP (`registerServeTools`).
- [ ] Documented in `docs/` alongside the existing tool reference and in the
      beads skill.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/tools/...` green; gofmt/vet/staticcheck clean.

title: Move world/lane vocabulary out of agent/subagent; drop the false import-cycle claim
description:
Evidence re-derived 2026-11-13. The original was stale within two days of filing, and its stated justification was wrong from the start.

THE CLAIM. internal/agent/runner/role_resolver.go:8-11 says SubAgentRoleResolver is "the bridge that lets the tools package access role metadata without importing agent/subagent, breaking the design-level import cycle (tools -> agent/subagent -> ...)". Both halves are false.

There is no cycle. internal/agent/subagent is a leaf: its only yaah imports are permissions, prompts and rolefile, and it does not import internal/tools. A tools -> agent/subagent edge is a downward dependency onto a leaf, not an upward reach; only the path prefix makes it look like one.

The cited evidence no longer exists. The five files named as importing agent/subagent for the world vocabulary (retained.go:24, proposal.go:9, dispatch_container.go:12, dispatch_authority.go:8, git_delta.go:22) moved out of internal/tools into internal/dispatch in yaah-5d85 on 2026-11-05, two days after this bead was filed. The only remaining tools -> agent/subagent imports are delegate_schema.go and list_subagents.go, and those are for DelegatableRoles — a different concern, tracked as yaah-4b5e.3.

THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM IS REAL AND BIGGER THAN FILED. internal/dispatch still imports agent/subagent, and every single use is world vocabulary — 60 references, all WorldContainer (20), WorldResolution (16), WorldWorktree (9), WorldAuto (4), WorldShared (3), WorldRequest (2), WorldKind (2), ResolveWorld (2), WorldAvailability (1), ErrWorldUnavailable (1), and nothing role-related at all. The import exists purely so dispatch can name a type. Two further packages outside agent/ depend on the same vocabulary: internal/doctor/checks.go and internal/worldinfo/worldinfo.go. So a domain vocabulary owned by the sub-agent package is being imported by three unrelated consumers.

STILL TO DO.
1. Move WorldContainer / WorldResolution and the rest of the world vocabulary (internal/agent/subagent/world.go) to a neutral package or internal/types, so dispatch, doctor and worldinfo stop importing agent/subagent for naming alone.
2. Rewrite the runner/role_resolver.go comment: drop the cycle claim and state what the adapter actually does — expose the global role registry through the tools.RoleResolver injection seam so DelegateTool and list_subagents stay testable without touching global state.

A sibling copy of the same false claim, in internal/tools/role_resolver.go, was already deleted in commit 4aca11dd on fix/hygiene-pass. This is the remaining instance.
