title: sqlite-vec (vec0) index for memory semantic search, replacing the in-Go brute-force scan
description:
# Replace the in-Go brute-force vector scan with a bundled sqlite-vec (vec0) index for memory search

Semantic memory search currently embeds the query, then scans every `memory` row with a non-null `embedding` BLOB and computes cosine similarity in Go (`internal/memory/memory_vector.go`, `SearchMemoryVectorScopedDiag`). That is correct and fast at current scale, but it hand-rolls an O(N) scan and duplicates what a vector index should provide.

`modernc.org/sqlite` (already a direct dependency, pinned v1.53.0) bundles `sqlite-vec` as the `modernc.org/sqlite/vec` subpackage — a CGo-free `vec0` virtual table for vector search inside the existing SQLite file. A single blank import auto-installs it via `sqlite3_auto_extension`. This keeps SQLite as the single source of truth while delegating the cosine scan to the DB: no external process, no CGo, no new storage engine.

This is greenfield: no existing DB data needs migrating; installs may nuke `state.db`.

Scope: memory (`memory_search` path) only. Message vector search (`SearchMessagesVector`) is an explicit follow-up, not part of this bead.

Why now: the spike (see Notes) de-risked every unknown — the extension is present at the pinned version, `EncodeEmbedding` is directly compatible, and `vec0` cosine distance equals `1 - CosineSimilarity` exactly. Remaining work is plumbing, with the dimension-pinning flow (see Design) as the only real design point.

title: vec0 (sqlite-vec) index for session message search (messages_vec)
description:
Follow-up to the closed yaah-f9bq (memory_vec index). Session message semantic search already exists (SearchMessagesVector brute-force scans messages.embedding, wired into memory_search_sessions), but messages grow unboundedly, so the O(N) scan is the one place semantic recall actually degrades at scale. Add a messages_vec vec0 virtual table mirroring messages.embedding, and dispatch SearchMessagesVector to it with the brute-force scan as fallback.

Scope: messages only. No new metadata filters — messages carry no scope/superseded tier, so the vec0 table holds just the embedding and the search joins back to messages for id+content (preserving the existing VectorResult{Entry{ID,Text}} shape).

Known pre-existing gap (out of scope): messages have no model-swap re-embed pass (unlike memory's ReembedStaleEmbeddings), so a model swap leaves message embeddings stale. The vec0 backfill copies only matching-width rows, so after a swap messages_vec stays empty until messages are re-written — same effective semantic-search outage as today, not a regression.

title: message model-swap re-embed pass (close the semantic-search outage)
description: Follow-up to yaah-8mxk (messages_vec index). Messages had no model-swap heal: after a model swap, message BLOBs stayed stale-width and messages_vec backfilled nothing, so session messages went semantically unsearchable (same outage as before the index, but now clearly a gap to close). Add the message-side counterpart to memory's ReembedStaleEmbeddings/ReconcileEmbeddings and wire it into the startup backfill.

title: Unified recall: one entry point spanning memory atoms and session messages
description:
Today recall is three silos the agent must choose between correctly: `memory_search` (distilled atoms, scope/tag filtered), `memory_search_sessions` (raw transcripts), and the `skill` tool's search action (capabilities). The failure mode is specific and real: the agent asks one surface, gets a weak or empty answer, and stops — even though the answer lives in another surface it never tried. The agent cannot reliably know up front which surface to ask, so the tool should decide.

This bead records the DECISION for a unified `recall` surface. The implementation is a follow-up feature bead once these choices are pinned — the plumbing (vec0 indexes, hybrid union, clean result shapes `Entry` / `MessageVectorResult`) is already in place from yaah-f9bq and yaah-8mxk.

## The hard problem is ranking heterogeneous evidence, not plumbing

The three kinds are evidence of different trust:

- a global memory atom is distilled and durable ("the user prefers X");
- a session message is a raw utterance ("I think I'd maybe prefer X");
- a session-scoped atom is between them.

Raw cosine does not know this. yaah already encodes the principle for atoms (scope + age rendering: "a durable global fact and a session atom from four days ago deserve different trust"); unified recall extends it across sources. Ranking purely by cosine risks a lexically-close raw message displacing a distilled fact — a recall regression, not an improvement.

title: spike: reproduce the greetz anomaly — untracked host files seeded into retained worktrees
description:
# Reproduce the greetz anomaly: untracked host files in a "fresh" worktree

Source: `.yaah/usage_reporting/2026-11-07-subagent-fork-continue-usage-report.md`, finding F9 (unverified, low confidence).

During a continue/fork demo, a "fresh" retained worktree for `internal/greetz` reported passing subtests before the sub-agent wrote its own test file; the sub-agent inferred a pre-existing `greetz_test.go` and overwrote it.

## Hypothesis

The retained lane seeds each worktree with `Apply(parent.CaptureWorkspace())`. The git backend's `Capture` stages into a scratch index with `git add -A`, so **untracked, non-ignored files in the host working tree are part of the captured state** and therefore appear in the "fresh" worktree. If the host tree held a stale untracked `internal/greetz/...` at dispatch time, the sub-agent would see it.

This is not necessarily a bug — the lane deliberately seeds the parent's exact state — but "fresh worktree" means fresh relative to the parent's current tree, including untracked content. The demo assumed otherwise.

Alternative cause: a stale `go test` cache returning prior package results. Confirm or rule out.

## Repro

1. Add an untracked file with a test to the host tree (e.g. `internal/greetz/greetz_test.go`).
2. Dispatch a proposal-lane sub-agent whose workdir would include it.
3. Assert whether the file is present in the seeded worktree and whether `go test` observes it.
4. Repeat with the file added to `.gitignore` to confirm it is NOT seeded.
5. Repeat on a clean host tree with a warm `go test` cache to test the cache hypothesis.

## Acceptance

- A test pins the seeding contract: tracked + untracked-not-ignored content seeds; ignored content does not.
- If the contract is intended, document it (the demo's "fresh" assumption was wrong) and note it in the retained-lane docs.
- If the anomaly was the test cache, record that and close.

title: feat(dispatch): opt-in seal-time hygiene checks on the sealed worktree
description:
Source: usage-report addendum §4.

A sub-agent whose `bash` is denied (`yaah-1tkp.1`) cannot run gofmt/vet; one dispatch escalated `info` documenting it. The host has the toolchain.

## Ask

An opt-in, per-role seal-time hygiene check: after sealing a worktree proposal, run `gofmt -l` / `go vet` (or configured commands) against the sealed worktree on the host and attach the result to the dispatch envelope. Worktree lane only — the container lane has no host toolchain. Integrate with `evidence_guard` / quality gates rather than adding a parallel mechanism.

## Notes

This treats a symptom: the better lever may be fixing read-only sub-agent shell (`yaah-1tkp.1`). Keep both.

## Acceptance

- Opt-in config; the result rides the dispatch envelope.
- Failures are advisory and never block sealing.
- No effect when disabled; the container-lane gap is documented.

title: feat(proposal): batch fork — N steering prompts, N branches
description:
Source: usage-report addendum §3.

Branching one parent forces sequential `fork` calls; racing two forks correctly yields `a continue/fork is already in progress`. The per-parent lock is right; the orchestrator wants to fan out.

## Ask

A fork form that accepts N steering prompts and seals N branches, acquiring the per-parent claim once. Define partial-failure semantics (all-or-nothing vs per-branch outcomes) and the envelope shape.

## Acceptance

- One call fans out to N branches atomically with respect to the per-parent claim.
- A failed branch is reported without stranding the others.
- Single-fork behavior is unchanged.
- Tests: success, partial failure, concurrent single fork (still refused).

title: feat(proposal): apply dry-run / merge-plan preview
description:
Source: usage-report addendum §8.

The conflict taxonomy is precomputed, but `apply`/`select` have no dry-run, so a drifted tree is committed blind.

## Ask

A preview that reports the merge plan — paths that land, which strategy applies (`select` fast-forward vs path-disjoint `apply` vs `three_way`), and which paths fail closed — without writing the parent or consuming the output. Reuse the existing analysis; keep it read-only.

## Acceptance

- Preview returns the same classification `apply` would act on.
- Nothing is written or consumed; the proposal stays open.
- Tests: clean tree, drifted tree, conflicting tree.

title: spike: handoff-summary seeding for cross-role continuation
description:
Source: usage-report addendum "nice-to-have" (cross-role handoff).

Cross-role conversation seeding is refused by design — a different role's system prompt/policy would leak. A distilled brief (the parent conversation compressed to a rationale summary attached to the new role's prompt) would capture most of the transfer value for `developer → golang-developer` style assembly lines.

## Ask

A spike/decision on a `seed_mode: summary` (or `handoff` param): summarize the source transcript in the source role's context, then seed the new role with the sealed workspace plus that summary. Consider cost (a summarizer call), fidelity, and how the summary is produced/validated.

## Acceptance

- A decision with adopt/decline and a design sketch, or a narrow implementation behind a flag.
- If adopted: the summary is produced deterministically enough to test, and the new role's system prompt is not leaked from the source.

title: Merge builtinPersonas into RoleRegistry (single role loader)
description:
internal/agent/subagent/persona.go re-parses the embedded role files, re-validates mode:primary, maintains its own built-in shadowing rule, and keeps a separate map. RoleRegistry.LoadBytes/LoadDir already does all of this. Two loaders mean two normalization paths (timing of normalization differs: persona.go:161-171 vs role_def.go) and a third explanation of "built-in wins".

Make build/plan ordinary registry entries and define a persona as a capability filter (mode primary|all). Personas() becomes a query, not a parallel construction.

Depends on yaah-21uk (primary-capable agents) settling the registry shape.

Acceptance: one loader, one normalization; build/plan still shadow user files; Personas() output byte-identical; golden tests unchanged.

title: Per-session permission ruleset + managed deny ceiling (OpenCode parity)
description:
Two opencode mechanisms yaah lacks:
1. Durable per-session narrowing (opencode Session.Info.permissions): a client can tighten a session without editing project/global config, persisted with the session row.
2. A policy hook that can only deny (opencode config/plugin/policy.ts): after user rules evaluate, an org/managed statement forces deny. yaah's nearest analogue is InheritedCeiling, which is sub-agent-only and limited to mutating file tools.

Add: (a) `session.permissions` (ruleset) accepted at create/update and by ACP, evaluated after agent rules and before saved approvals; (b) a managed deny layer evaluated last, deny-only, with a message.

Acceptance: session narrowing survives resume and is enforced by the same evaluator; managed layer can force deny but never allow; managed deny cannot be overridden by yolo/saved approvals; tests + docs.

title: acp: surface the question tool as ACP elicitation instead of auto-answering
description: internal/acp/server.go:53-56 sets AutoAnswerQuestions with the rationale 'ACP has no interactive question surface in Tier 1 (elicitation is a future capability)', and server.go:217-221 answers the question tool with the first option. A question that changes behaviour - which file to edit, which deploy target, which of three options - is silently resolved by yaah instead of the human.  This is the most user-visible correctness gap in the ACP surface: the answer is wrong with no signal that anything was decided.  Implement elicitation: - send the question to the client and block the turn until the client answers - use the same request/response plumbing as session/request_permission (internal/acp/approval.go) - resolve by JSON-RPC id, with a bound and a timeout outcome - map the question's options onto the client's selectable options, preserving order and the default - define the timeout / cancel outcome (the spec has a cancelled outcome for an unanswered elicitation - note that internal/acp/approval.go:169-174 already documents deviating from that for permissions, so be deliberate about the same choice here) - drop the AutoAnswerQuestions default once elicitation works, or keep it as an explicit opt-out flag

title: beads: repair the local beads workspace (stale bd binary, wrong storage mode, Dolt version mismatch)
description:
The local beads workspace was broken for bd clients on this machine and needed a manual repair on 2026-10-21. Two independent faults:

1. Stale bd binary. The installed bd was built from an older source and only knows schema version 53, while the shared database is at v66. Reads need BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 to work at all, and writes fail outright with 'table not found: events'. Fixed by reinstalling:
   CGO_ENABLED=0 go install -tags gms_pure_go github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@latest
   (this produced bd 1.3.1 (dev) and cleared the skew)

2. Wrong storage mode. .beads/metadata.json had dolt_mode: embedded, which the CGO_ENABLED=0 binary cannot use. The dolt sql-server was already running (PID 44964, port 57124) but the 'yaah' database was missing from it, and the server log shows a continuous 'database not found: yaah' error since 2026-10-19 - so every bd command in this workspace had been failing for days. Fixed by setting dolt_mode to 'server' in .beads/metadata.json and running 'bd bootstrap' to clone the database from the configured remote (https://doltremoteapi.dolthub.com/buchenberg/yaah).

What is needed to stop this recurring:
- document the CGO_ENABLED=0 install line for bd in AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md, since the default install on Windows produces a binary that cannot open the database
- decide whether dolt_mode: server should be committed to .beads/metadata.json (it is currently a local working-tree change) or left per-machine
- note the installed Dolt binary is old (1.x - no 'dolt sql-client', no 'dolt --version'), while bd expects a 2.x-style multi-database data dir; bd's own server lifecycle works around this but the mismatch is a landmine

Also worth fixing: 'beads.role' is not configured, so every bd command prints a GH#2950 warning.

Related: the dolt-server-lifecycle skill documents the external server mode (~/.dolt-servers/yaah, port 3306) but the workspace is actually using bd's own per-project server (.beads/dolt-server.pid / .port). The skill and the workspace layout disagree.

title: Route container sessions through the goatherd sandbox seam (sandbox/croft adapter)
description:
# Route container sessions through the goatherd sandbox seam (`sandbox/croft` adapter)

## Context

yaah has two workspace lanes today, wired through **different seams**:

- **Local session (default)**: sub-agents fork a git worktree via
  goatherd-runtime's `sandbox/git` backend (`internal/agent/runner/runner.go:1013`,
  `mgr.ForkIsolated(..., goatherdgit.NewWorktreeSandbox(...))`) with
  Landlock/winacl paddocks. Retained proposals + settlement active
  (`cmd/yaah/wiring.go:736`: `Retain: sessionSandbox == nil && ...`).
- **Container session** (`workspace.backend: containerd`,
  `internal/config/workspace.go:20`): the whole session runs inside a croft
  sandbox, constructed **directly** by yaah — `tools.OpenContainerdWorkspaceSandbox`
  (`internal/tools/workspace_probe.go`) via
  `tools.StartSessionSandbox(...)` (`wiring.go:302-309`). This lane bypasses
  goatherd-runtime's `Sandbox` registry entirely, and `Retain` is off.

Two concrete problems with the current shape:

1. **Stale pin / API drift.** `go.mod` requires the pre-rename
   `github.com/buchenberg/croft v0.3.0` while goatherd-croft is at **v0.8.0**
   (module `github.com/buchenberg/goatherd-croft`). yaah calls API removed in
   v0.4.0: `croft.SandboxSpec`, `croft.ContainContained`,
   `croft.CanonicalDigest`, `WorkspaceState.Backend`, `Diff(ctx, ws, maxLines)`.
2. **Structural asymmetry.** The container lane can never gain runtime
   semantics (capture digests, `DeltaApplier`, settlement, recovery) because it
   never flows through the seam where those live.

Architectural framing (see `croft-shepherd-fit.md` in the Frameworks dir):
croft is a **world** (substrate axis, sibling of `sandbox/git` under
`sandbox.Sandbox`) — not a paddock (`containment.Backend`, where landlock/
winacl live). In the Shepherd reference, carriers sit behind the substrate
seam; the framework stays dep-light. The fix is an adapter, not a copy and
not a merge: croft stays standalone.

## Plan

### Phase 0 — upstream adapter (goatherd-runtime repo; file a companion bead there; blocks this bead)

Create nested module **`goatherd-runtime/sandbox/croft`** (own `go.mod` +
version stream, requires root runtime + kernel — the `sandbox/landlock` /
`sandbox/winacl` packaging precedent), pinning `goatherd-croft v0.8.0+`:

1. Implement `sandbox.Sandbox`:
   - `Backend() = "containerd"`; `RegisterSandbox("containerd", factory)`.
   - Factory takes an **adapter-owned** `Config` type (wrapping the croft
     essentials: Address, Namespace, Image, Runtime, Snapshotter, Workdir,
     Limits, Network, Secrets, StagingDir, output caps) so hosts never import
     croft types. Unknown config fails loudly (registry convention).
   - `Create/Destroy` → croft lifecycle; `Exec` maps runtime `ExecRequest` →
     croft exec with a real deadline ceiling per the Sandbox contract;
     `ReadFile/WriteFile`; `Diff` from croft's daemon change-set blobs.
2. **Digest-stable `Capture`**: content-hash the four-field croft
   `WorkspaceState` (`sha256(SnapshotKey‖ParentKey‖BaseKey‖Image)`, as
   croft-broker does) so identical content yields equal digests; record the
   residual sequence-key gap in the adapter docs, per the `Sandbox.Capture`
   contract's own instruction.
3. **Honest capabilities**: `Lifecycle/Exec/FileIO/Diff/Isolated = true`;
   `Containment = contained` (container boundary, not syscall tier — never
   claim paddock-class enforcement; do NOT attempt Landlock inside the
   container, seccomp may block it and it's redundant).
4. Implement optional **`DeltaApplier`** via croft `ApplyDelta`;
   `ErrDeltaConflict` propagates so settlement's apply verb fails closed.
5. Do **not** implement `Addressed` (croft identity is not a path; container
   recovery adoption stays a recorded follow-up).
6. Tests in the runtime: digest-stability property test, capabilities honesty,
   registry resolution + unknown-config failure, `ApplyDelta` conflict path;
   env-gated live tests reusing croft's `CROFT_CONTAINERD_ADDR` harness.
7. Out of scope for v0.1: `effect.FromChanges([]croft.Change)` extraction
   (runtime plan 05) — but expose `Changes` on the adapter for it.

### Phase 1 — yaah rewiring

1. Replace `tools.OpenContainerdWorkspaceSandbox`'s direct croft construction
   with `sandbox.OpenSandbox("containerd", croftadapter.Config{...})`
   (blank-import the nested module for registration).
2. Update `SandboxOpener` (`internal/tools/workspace_lifecycle.go`) and
   `workspace_probe.go` / `workspace_bootstrap.go` to the adapter config.
3. **Drop** `github.com/buchenberg/croft v0.3.0` from `go.mod`; require
   `goatherd-runtime/sandbox/croft` (which brings goatherd-croft v0.8.0+).
   Migrate removed-API call sites (`SandboxSpec`→`Config`, no
   `CanonicalDigest`/`ContainContained`/`WorkspaceState.Backend`, new `Diff`
   signature) — all inside the adapter, none in yaah.
4. Rework `internal/sandboxfake` to double the adapter seam (or keep doubling
   `croft.Sandbox` and exercise it through the adapter).
5. **Keep the `Retain` gate unchanged** (`sessionSandbox == nil && ...`):
   container sessions still produce no retained outputs in this phase.
6. `internal/doctor/checks.go` croft check probes via the adapter (containerd
   reachable, image resolvable).

### Phase 2 — verification

1. Unit: registry resolution, config mismatch fails loudly, digest stability,
   capabilities honesty, conflict → apply-refusal.
2. Env-gated live (`CROFT_CONTAINERD_ADDR`, root): full session lifecycle
   through the seam — `StartSessionSandbox` → exec → file IO → capture →
   apply → destroy — with behavior parity vs the old direct lane.
3. Bench: run the `orch-confinement` terminal-bench task under a
   container-session config to prove the boundary still holds end-to-end.

### Phase 3 — optional follow-up (separate bead; do not block this one)

Retained outputs in container mode: with croft behind the `Sandbox` seam,
`ForkIsolated`-style proposals over container state diffs become structurally
possible. Gate behind an experiment flag; default stays Retain-off.

**HARD BLOCKER: goatherd-croft bead `croft-dlb` must land first.** Settlement's
`select` verb compares `trace.WorkspaceState` digests *as content equality*.
Croft states are sequence-keyed, so two captures of an unchanged workspace
digest differently and `select` would misfire. Until `croft-dlb` ships the
no-change capture fast path + an exposed `ContentDigest`, the Retain gate
(`sessionSandbox == nil && ...`, `cmd/yaah/wiring.go:736`) is the only thing
keeping settlement off container states. Turning Retain on without `croft-dlb`
breaks that invariant. Phases 1-2 are unaffected — they keep Retain off.

## Acceptance

- `grep -r 'buchenberg/croft'` in yaah returns nothing; the only croft module
  in the graph is `goatherd-croft v0.8.0+` via `goatherd-runtime/sandbox/croft`.
- `workspace.backend: containerd` sessions work end-to-end through
  `OpenSandbox("containerd")` with parity to the current direct lane (tool
  exec, file IO, lifecycle, teardown).
- Sandbox-contract tests pass in the adapter (digest stability, honest
  capabilities, fail-closed registry).
- Local git-worktree lane is untouched (no behavior change; `Retain` gate as-is).
- `yaah doctor` container check green; `orch-confinement` container arm green.

## Risks & open questions

- **Digest-stability residual — corrected.** The originally planned interim
  (content-hash the four-field croft state, the croft-broker scheme) does
  **not** cover "same content, new capture": `SnapshotKey` is sequence-derived,
  so re-capturing unchanged content yields a new key and a new hash. The broker
  scheme is a stable *name* for a state, not content equality. The adapter
  therefore does not hand-roll a hash — `trace.WorkspaceState.Digest()` already
  canonicalizes deterministically — and records the gap per the `Capture`
  contract's own instruction. Real fix is `croft-dlb`; it gates Phase 3 only.
  Settlement consumes `trace.WorkspaceState` digests, never raw croft keys —
  still confirm during Phase 2.
- **Egress interplay**: croft's netns (loopback-only default) is the container
  lane's egress answer; document how it coexists with the `egress` posture
  vocabulary (`allow_all`/`deny_all`/`broker`) so config isn't ambiguous.
- **Version skew**: adapter is a new version stream (start v0.1.0) requiring
  runtime v0.19.0+; yaah pins the adapter. The stale-pin problem must not
  recur — prefer bumping the adapter with croft minors.
- **SessionSandbox lifecycle mapping**: `StartSessionSandbox` semantics
  (long-lived session world vs per-scope fork) must map cleanly onto
  `Create`/`Destroy`; verify the concurrency contract (croft's opMu) matches
  session usage.

## References

- `croft-shepherd-fit.md` (Frameworks dir) — the two-axes analysis and diagrams
- `yaah-shepherd-gap-report.md` §5.2 item 4, §7.2 item 1 (container tier)
- goatherd-runtime `docs/plans/05-container-tier.md` (effect extraction),
  `docs/plans/07-yaah-integration.md`
- goatherd-runtime `sandbox/sandbox.go` (Sandbox contract, Capture digest
  stability, DeltaApplier), `sandbox/containment/backend.go` (paddock family)
- Companion bead to file in goatherd-runtime for Phase 0.

title: trace: record message-content facts so trace.db can reconstruct sessions
description:
Today trace.db holds the orchestrating agent's skeleton only: tool declaration/capture pairs (args but no output bodies), turn lifecycle facts (turn:created carries the full prompt; completed carries token counts), and per-turn frontiers. Assistant response text, reasoning content + signature, tool result bodies, and the system prompt are absent — so a session cannot be reconstructed from the trace, and sub-agent transcripts are entirely ephemeral (subagent_loop.go skips persistence; only the final delegate result survives in the parent transcript).

Extend ShepherdTraceMiddleware (internal/agent/pipeline/trace.go) with three content-fact types, appended through the existing Append path (no kernel change needed):

1. assistant-response capture per model turn — content, reasoning_content, reasoning_signature (signature required for Anthropic thinking replay on resume; see bd memory anthropic-sdk-go-v1-81-0-requires-signature)
2. tool-output capture — truncated body or spill-file reference, reusing the existing ToolResultMaxBytes/spill-dir truncation point (the kernel has no payload cap; the 64KiB session-prompt cap is the precedent for ours)
3. session-context fact at session start — system prompt (capped), cwd, model/config fingerprint. While here, stamp per-dispatch RetainedContext for sub-agents (substrate=worktree, containment=jail posture, capability refs=role tool belt) so authority provenance is digest-bound rather than living only in mutable sessions.workspace_backend columns.

Payoffs: crash-safe session mirror (the kernel intent ledger closes the 33ms debounce window), compaction can become cuts instead of destructive rebase, and sub-agent intermediate work becomes durable under synthetic owners (joinable via trace_owners).

Non-goals: replacing state.db (FTS5, embeddings, session pagination stay there) and co-locating the stores (blocked on kernel TraceStore interface per .agents/plans/consolidate-persistence).

Background research: Frameworks/goatherd-yaah-storage-delta-report.md (deltas 4.1-4.5, witness section).

## Context
Derived from 2026-10-22 deep-dive comparing goatherd-kernel causal-DAG storage vs yaah state.db (goatherd-yaah-storage-delta-report.md). Related shipped work: consolidate-persistence cross-link phase (messages.trace_id/turn_id, trace_owners).

title: consolidate: dedupe atoms against existing memory (skip near-dupes, merge stale)
description:
The consolidator deep-sleep directive said "write durable atoms" but never checked existing memory first. With consolidate_turns_interval=3 each nudge hands the consolidator a bounded tail (16 msgs / 8000 bytes), so consecutive runs see overlapping context and re-persist the same facts as near-duplicate atoms.

Observed 2026-10-22 in session sess-1792696158210007248: 3 consolidator runs produced 17 raw facts -> 8 atoms, with 3 near-dupe clusters (2x sub-agent pipeline wiring, 2x Threadlines install, 2x beads P1 list). memory_add's exact-match dedup does not catch semantic near-duplicates.

Fix:
- consolidateDirective now leads with a dedupe pass: memory_search first, skip facts already stored, memory_update stale/partial atoms, memory_add only when nothing covers it.
- consolidator role gains memory_update (tools list + prompt rule).
- runner registers MemoryUpdateTool for the consolidator role (DB-backed tools are otherwise silently dropped for sub-agents; memory_update was missing from the switch alongside memory_add/memory_search).

Validation: go build ./... clean; go test ./cmd/yaah ./internal/agent/runner ./internal/tools green.

title: revisit compaction-as-sleep analogy — honest memory optimization framing
description:
The sleep analogy (light/deep sleep, consolidation=nudge) is useful but may be over-extended. Consolidation is just consolidation; equating it to sleep is a stretch. The README's compaction section should describe memory optimization benefits and mechanics honestly, not force the sleep metaphor. Need to:
- Re-evaluate the analogy in docs/compaction-as-sleep.md
- Rewrite README section to focus on: context compaction (summarization), scheduled consolidation (durable memory extraction), and their distinct triggers (pressure vs cadence)
- Document actual implementation: CompactionMiddleware (reactive, overflow-driven) + ConsolidateMiddleware (proactive, cadence-driven) + consolidator sub-agent (restricted toolset, sealed proposals)
- Keep useful concepts (boundary-aware compaction, scheduled consolidation, guardrails) but drop forced sleep terminology

title: release: publish per-platform archives with registry-canonical keys + sha256
description:
The registry manifest requires distribution.binary with a per-platform archive map. Publish GoReleaser (or equivalent) artifacts and record checksums.

EXACT platform keys required by agent.schema.json / PLATFORM_MAP (verify_agents.py:43-50) — note aarch64, NOT arm64:
  darwin-aarch64, darwin-x86_64, linux-aarch64, linux-x86_64, windows-aarch64, windows-x86_64
A missing/mismatched key fails with 'no archive for current platform'.

ARCHIVE LAYOUT (Medium): verify_binary extracts the archive then runs resolve_binary_executable(extract_dir, cmd), resolving cmd relative to the EXTRACT ROOT (verify_agents.py:504-518). A tarball nesting everything under yaah-<ver>-linux-x86_64/ will fail unless cmd names the nested path. Prefer flat archives so cmd can be './yaah' (and './yaah.exe' on Windows).

SHA256 (Medium): sha256 is OPTIONAL in the schema (correcting an earlier assumption), but if present it must be 64 lowercase hex and is VERIFIED — a mismatch deletes the cached archive and hard-fails the run. Generate per-platform checksums correctly or omit the field entirely.

Windows archives should be .zip; Unix .tar.gz.

title: memory: make session atoms retrievable, promotable, and self-correcting
description:
The consolidation middleware works: the memory store holds 137 atoms, all with embeddings and digests, all FTS-indexed, partitioned across 4 sessions. The tiered scope design is also deliberate and documented. But the retrieval and lifecycle sides have three gaps that together make the feature much less useful than it looks, and one of them was actively misleading.

OBSERVED STATE (2026-10-23, ~/.yaah/state.db):
  global   atoms: 1
  session  atoms: 136
  promote/supersede helpers in internal/memory or internal/agent: none (grep)

(1) SESSION ATOMS ARE UNREACHABLE
internal/tools/memory.go:20 documents Scope on MemorySearchTool: "Empty means
ScopeGlobal: session-scoped atoms are working-context and must not leak into a
default (cross-session) recall; a caller that wants them sets Scope explicitly."
But the exposed memory_search schema accepts only query/tag/top_k (memory.go:10-12,
:24-26) - there is no `scope` parameter. So nothing can set Scope, and the 136
session atoms are write-only: no later session can retrieve them.
Evidence that this is a schema gap and not a ranking problem: searching the literal
token "typeahead", which appears verbatim in the newest session atom, returned the
unrelated single global atom, not the typeahead atom.

(2) NOTHING PROMOTES DURABLE FACTS TO GLOBAL
The global tier grew to exactly one atom, by luck rather than by mechanism. Hard-won
cross-session facts from a single long session - that sub-agents with a blocked shell
report work they did not do; that Alpine needs 'unsafe-eval' in a CSP or the page is
inert; that the ACP registry auth check defaults a missing "type" to "agent" - were
all consolidated into session scope and are now stranded. Session atoms are supposed
to be working context, but nothing ever decides a fact has stopped being context.

(3) NO SUPERSESSION, SO GLOBAL ATOMS GO STALE SILENTLY
The one global atom asserted "yaah currently returns authMethods: [] ... No bead
tracks this", both false by the time it was read: three static agent-typed methods
shipped in v0.102.0 and yaah-ap7/yaah-aon track the work. Because default recall can
return only global atoms, that made a confident falsehood the sole recalled fact for
every new session in this repo. It was corrected by hand during inspection. A wrong
global memory is worse than a missing one: it is asserted with authority and nothing
in the store marks it as contested or outdated.

PROPOSED (in value order)
1. Expose `scope` in the memory_search schema (the implementation already supports it;
   this is a schema-only change) so session atoms are at least inspectable per session.
2. Give durable facts a route to the global tier: have the consolidator emit
   scope:"global" for cross-session truths, and/or add a memory_promote that moves or
   copies an atom up a tier with a reason.
3. Supersede on write: when a new atom contradicts an existing global atom, replace it
   or mark it superseded, so the store cannot accumulate confident falsehoods.

title: fallback swap into thinking-mode provider replays thinking-less history, 400 aborts run with misleading advice
description:
## Symptom

Mid-session provider fallback (openrouter `recursive/flint-v1.0:free` → `deepseek/deepseek-flash`) aborts the run:

    error: provider error [deepseek/deepseek-flash]: model "deepseek-flash" requires thinking
    mode but reasoning_content was omitted — set `thinking: true` for this model in config:
    provider returned 400: The `content[].thinking` in the thinking mode must be passed back
    to the API. (request_id: a04e93ba-89e0-4d3c-b266-ebf125c25328)

The canned advice is wrong for this case: `thinking: true` was **already set** for
deepseek-flash in `~/.yaah/config.yaml`. Observed in session
`sess-1792783060339910427` (bd yaah-78t run, 2026-10-23).

## Root cause

1. Primary request fails (429/degenerate stream/premature close — not recorded in
   trace.db). `Client.swapToFallback` (internal/agent/llm/client.go) rotates to the
   fallback **mid-run** and replays the same request, full history included.
2. All assistant messages in that history were produced by the primary over the
   OpenAI-compatible path: `reasoning_content=""`, `reasoning_signature=""`.
3. DeepSeek serves `deepseek-flash` in thinking mode server-side. Its
   Anthropic-compatible endpoint requires thinking blocks to be passed back on
   replayed assistant turns. `lowerAnthropicRequest` (internal/providers/anthropic.go)
   correctly omits thinking blocks when no signature was captured (fabricating one
   is rejected), so the request is missing `content[].thinking` → 400.
4. `errorclassify.Classify` matches "must be passed back" + "thinking" →
   `ReasonThinkingModeRequired`, `ShouldAbort=true`, with the
   "set `thinking: true`" message template. That template conflates two distinct
   failures: (a) model requires thinking mode but the *response* omitted reasoning
   (config fix applies) and (b) provider demands thinking blocks be *replayed* but
   the history has none because it came from a different, non-thinking provider
   (no config fix applies).

Sessions that ran on deepseek-flash from turn 0 work fine — every assistant message
carries a DeepSeek-issued signature, so replays are valid. The failure is specific to
a mid-conversation swap into a thinking-mode Anthropic-dialect provider with foreign
history. No automatic recovery exists: `ShouldStripReasoning` does not apply (the
field is not the problem — missing blocks are, and they cannot be fabricated).

## Fix direction

In the fallback path, detect the incompatible combination: swapped-to provider is a
thinking model (registry or `thinking: true` config) while the replayed history
contains assistant turns with empty `reasoning_signature`. Then either:

- trim the replayed history back to the last user message (loses in-flight tool
  state but keeps the turn alive on the fallback), or
- fail the swap fast with an accurate message ("fallback provider X requires
  thinking replay; history originates from non-thinking provider Y").

Also split the classifier message for `ReasonThinkingModeRequired` so case (b)
reports the provider-swap cause instead of the `thinking: true` config hint.

title: ACP: advertise a model picker via configOptions + session/set_config_option
description:
## Problem

In Zed, an ACP agent connected to `yaah acp-serve` has **no model selector**. The
same Zed panel connected to GLM's ACP agent shows one. Users must edit
`~/.yaah/config.yaml` and restart the agent process to change models, while every
other yaah surface (TUI, web UI) can switch models live.

This is a **protocol-surface gap, not a capability gap**: `agentSession.SetModel`
exists (`cmd/yaah/session.go:652`), the TUI wires it to a picker
(`cmd/yaah/tui.go:120`), and the web UI exposes it. ACP simply never tells the
client that models exist to choose from.

## Root cause (verified)

| Fact | Location |
|---|---|
| `SessionNewResult` is `{sessionId}` only — no `configOptions`, no model advertisement | `internal/acp/protocol.go:131` |
| `session/load` responds with the same shape | `internal/acp/server.go:430` |
| Dispatch handles `initialize`, `authenticate`, `session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/load`, `session/set_mode` — **no `session/set_config_option`** | `internal/acp/server.go:742-780` |
| The `Session` interface the protocol layer depends on has no model accessor or mutator, so the plumbing is absent at this boundary | `internal/acp/server.go:30` |
| `session/set_mode` is a deliberate no-op ack (documented), which is why Zed's *mode* picker doesn't hang — a different picker that does nothing | `internal/acp/server.go:777`, `handleSetMode` at `:833`, `docs/acp.md` |
| Model is resolved process-wide from config at session build time; no per-session override reaches ACP | `cmd/yaah/acp_cmd.go`, `cmd/yaah/session.go` |

## ACP contract to satisfy (v1)

Source: <https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/schema>

- `session/new` and `session/load` results MAY carry `configOptions: SessionConfigOption[]`.
- `SessionConfigOption` = `{ id (required), name (required), description?, category?, type, currentValue, options }`.
  A dropdown is the **select** variant: `currentValue` (required) + `options`
  (`SessionConfigSelectOptions`: flat array of `{value, name, description?}`, or grouped arrays).
- `category: "model"` is the spec-reserved semantic category Zed renders as its
  model selector. Clients MUST handle missing/unknown categories gracefully, so
  advertising it is safe for clients that ignore it.
- The client changes a value with `session/set_config_option`, params
  `{sessionId, configId, value}`. The response MUST include `configOptions`:
  *"The full set of configuration options and their current values."*
- The agent MAY push `session/update` with `sessionUpdate: "config_option_update"`
  carrying the full `configOptions`, to push late/refreshed values.
- There is **no** legacy `models`/`availableModels` field in the current schema —
  `configOptions` is the only mechanism. (Verified: zero occurrences in the v1 schema.)

## Why this is worth doing

- Surface parity: TUI and web can switch models; ACP is the only surface that cannot.
- Removing a config-file-edit-and-restart loop for every model change.
- Cheap: `SetModel` already handles the hard part (provider rebuild + cache
  invalidation for compact/fallback providers). What's missing is ~200 lines of
  protocol plumbing plus a model catalog injection.

title: ACP: fs/read_text_file + fs/write_text_file bridge (unsaved editor buffer awareness)

title: replace reports partial application as success and truncation hides the failures
description: internal/tools/replace.go (~:186-208): per-file write/read errors are collected into fileResult entries that feed the SAME success message ("Replaced N match(es) across M file(s)") and Execute returns nil error. The message is then hard-truncated at replaceMaxResultLen, so on a wide replacement the error lines are exactly what gets cut. The model cannot distinguish a clean sweep from a half-applied one.

title: json_query delete of an array element claims removal but leaves null

title: read.md documents byte semantics for a line-based tool and promises metadata it never returns
description: internal/prompts/tools/read.md says offset is a "byte offset" and limit "max bytes" and that the tool returns "file contents along with metadata", but read.go splits on newline and treats offset/limit as lines (matching the JSON schema "Line number to start (1-based)"/"Maximum number of lines") and returns bare content. title: read: offset past EOF returns empty content with no error and limit truncation is unmarked
description: internal/tools/read.go (~:84-87): start > len(lines) returns "", nil — an out-of-range offset is indistinguishable from a zero-length file, so a model paginating past the end concludes the file is empty. A limit that cuts the file appends no truncation notice, unlike grep/glob/ls which do, so a truncated read looks complete.

title: diff stats drop any added/removed line whose content starts with a space; mode enum unvalidated
description: internal/tools/diff.go (parseDiffStats) excludes "+ "/"- " prefixed lines to skip file headers, which also discards real content lines whose text begins with a space (YAML, Markdown, indented literals). A change set touching only such lines reports files_changed:1, insertions:0, deletions:0 and the model concludes nothing changed. Also mode is not validated (anything != "unified" silently becomes git mode). No diff_test.go covers either.

title: background_process start failure returns nil error — failed launch reported as a successful tool call
description: internal/tools/background_process.go (~:61-67): when Manager.Start fails, start alone returns fmt.Sprintf("Failed to start process: %v", err), nil — every other action in the file returns a real Go error. The tool-result contract sees error==nil so approvals/telemetry record success for a process that never launched; Info is discarded too so the model cannot report a process id.

title: bisect: auto-run abort leaves status "in_progress" — model keeps marking a dead bisect
description: internal/tools/bisect.go (~:171-181): when runBisectTest fails, git bisect run aborts the whole bisect (exit 125/126/127 semantics preserved deliberately at :263), but result.Status is never changed and stays "in_progress" with empty bad_commit. The model reads "still bisecting" and keeps issuing good/bad against a terminated bisect. Only the missing-ref path sets status error.

title: bisect schema advertises test_cmd for good/bad but doMark silently drops it
description: internal/tools/bisect.go:37-39: the test_cmd schema description promises "Can also be used with good/bad to run one step", but doMark (~:184) ignores the argument (the code comment admits it was never implemented). A model that supplies test_cmd with good gets a plain mark with no test run and no indication the argument was dropped — it can conclude a fix candidate is good when nothing was tested.

title: go_mod discards the go error text for every action except tidy; post-mutation tidy failure swallowed
description: internal/tools/go_mod.go (~:56-60, :186-193): runGo drops res.Stderr, and only runTidy sets result.Stderr; verify/graph/list/why/add/remove/upgrade yield success:false with empty output AND empty stderr — a failed module operation with no cause. In runRemove/runUpgrade the follow-up tidy error path writes tidy stdout and drops tidyErr, while result.Success still says the mutation succeeded.

title: git commit silently drops the paths argument (over-broad commit reported as success)
description: internal/tools/git.go (~:206-210): commit builds "git commit -m msg" and ignores params.Paths entirely, though paths is a documented schema input and add uses it. A caller asking to commit only a.go commits whatever is staged, with no error and no note — unlike validateFlags which at least rejects silently-ignored flags for dangerous actions.

title: git pre-flights the binary on the host PATH so isolated workspaces are told "is git installed?"
description: internal/tools/git.go (~:146-148) resolves git with exec.LookPath on the host before executing through the workspace, while staticcheck.go:139 has a comment explaining exactly why that is wrong ("that is the wrong machine once a workspace can be isolated") and uses executableExit classification instead. Inside a substrate that ships git but whose host PATH lacks it, every git action fails with a confidently wrong "is git installed?".

title: git.md says fetch is gated by approval; the danger table classifies it read-only (two sources of truth)
description: internal/prompts/tools/git.md states "mutating actions (add, commit, push, pull, fetch) require approval", but git.go:28 allowedGitActions marks fetch read-only (dangerous:false, pinned by git_test.go:73). The doc and the approval gate disagree about the same action, and the doc is the only place the model learns what is gated. Note the same table also calls branch read-only while branch deletes branches (separate bead).

title: background_process log buffer silently drops the TAIL — the most recent output is what gets discarded
description: internal/process/process.go (~:45-58): the 200KB log cap keeps the first 200KB and discards everything after with no marker, so for a long-running server/build the diagnostic recent output is the part thrown away while a stale prefix is returned as if complete. background_process.go logs also returns "(no output yet)" both for a process that produced nothing and one whose output was lost — indistinguishable.

title: question returns an empty successful result on EOF — the question never reached a human
description: internal/tools/question.go (defaultQuestionHandler/Execute): when stdin reaches EOF (one-shot with closed stdin, serve/acp-serve, piped invocation, Ctrl-D) scanner.Scan fails, the loop breaks and Execute returns "" with nil error. The model sees a successful call with empty content — indistinguishable from "the user answered nothing" — and proceeds on a guess. Partial reads (EOF between questions) likewise return unqualified success.

title: todowrite accepts any status string; unrecognised status silently drops the item from every count
description: internal/tools/todo.go (Execute): the schema declares a status enum but Execute never validates it, so "done"/"blocked"/"in-progress" is stored verbatim and counted in nothing. The summary then reads "3 total, 0 completed, 0 in progress, 0 pending" — a self-contradicting string that looks like a successful write, and downstream renderers meet a status they have no case for.

title: memory_search.md still does not disclose that supplying tag forces keyword-only FTS search
description: internal/tools/memory.go (~:77): the vector path runs only when params.Tag == "" — any non-empty tag silently withdraws semantic recall and falls to SearchMemoryScoped (FTS5), yet internal/prompts/tools/memory_search.md:1,5 promises "semantic vector search that understands paraphrases" with tag presented as an orthogonal filter and the only stated fallback being "no embedding server available". The consolidate directive and consolidator role surfaces of this three-surface defect were fixed; the tool-doc surface is still live.

title: role tool: unvalidated role name reaches filepath.Join — ../ escapes the roles directory on create/delete
description: internal/tools/role.go: createRole/deleteRole interpolate the name straight into filepath.Join(dir, name+".md") with only non-emptiness validated. {action:create, name:"../../NOTES"} lands at <repo>/NOTES.md via atomicWriteFile and the same trick through delete removes an arbitrary .md the tool never advertised — all while reporting success. (Whether skills.Create/plans.Create validate their names was not verified in this audit.)

title: released-proposal teardown failure is swallowed and the record deleted — worktree stranded with no recovery path
description: internal/tools/retained.go (~:369): teardownReleasedProposal best-effort discards with _ = parent.Discard(scope), then the caller deletes the proposal from the registry and returns the envelope with no Error note. The orchestrator sees "settled" and proposal list no longer shows the id; the leftover worktree under .yaah/shepherd-worktrees/ is then only removable by hand. Contrast the report lane which at least slog.Warns.

title: subagent_jobs wait/status can never return the sub-agent output, and timed_out is an invented undocumented status
description: internal/tools/subagent_jobs.go:170 invents status "timed_out" (not in jobs.BackgroundJobStatus constants running|completed|failed|cancelled, and not in subagent_jobs.md), while the stored job stays running so the read-back is a lie about the registry. jobs.BackgroundJobStatus carries no result field, so a completed wait returns no work product either — the model must rely on a follow-up message it may already have consumed.

title: subagent_jobs wait ignores the caller context — a cancelled turn still blocks up to 300s
description: internal/tools/subagent_jobs.go:166 executeWait discards its ctx parameter and derives from context.Background(), so user abort, parent deadline or jail teardown cannot interrupt a wait; the tool spins until the 300s schema max even when the job was already cancelled by that abort.

title: delegate max_turns and output_limit are unclamped — schema bounds are advisory only
description: internal/tools/delegate.go (~:236-239): max_iterations gets clampMaxLoopCycles and timeout_seconds gets clampTimeoutSeconds, but MaxTurns (schema maximum 50) and OutputLimit (schema minimum 1024) are passed raw to the runner/jobs layer, so an injected payload can send negative or 10^6. The delegate.md promise "cannot go below the role min_turns" is enforced nowhere in this layer.

title: proposal and supervisor are model-facing tools with no embedded docs; descriptions are inline Go strings
description: internal/prompts/tools/ has delegate.md, subagent_jobs.md, list_subagents.md, question.md but no proposal.md or supervisor.md; both tools build their Description inline (proposal.go:20-22, supervisor.go:64-65) instead of prompts.ToolDescription, making them the only model-visible orchestration tools whose prose lives in Go literals — exactly the two with the most multi-verb behaviour (retained settlement; supervision status). Related: doc filenames are keyed by the ToolDescription arg, not Name(), so todowrite resolves via "todo" and memory_search_sessions via "memory_session_search" — an easy way to add a doc that is never embedded.

title: proposal list uses a process-global registry — cross-session leakage under web/acp-serve, prose output for list
description: internal/tools/retained.go:96 keeps retainedProposals in a process-global map and ProposalTool is instantiated with no session field (wiring.go:835), so under yaah web/acp-serve a session can list, show, select or discard ANOTHER session proposal (show prints its diff). list also returns bare prose ("No open proposals.") while show/settle return JSON envelopes, so "no proposals" is indistinguishable from a parse failure.

title: SSRF blocklist does not block 0.0.0.0/8 — on Linux it connects to loopback, bypassing the loopback guard
description: internal/tools/urlguard.go:20-31 blockedCIDRs lists 127.0.0.0/8, RFC-1918, link-local and IPv6 equivalents, but omits 0.0.0.0/8 (and 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT, 192.0.0.0/24, ::/128). On Linux connect(2) to 0.0.0.0 routes to 127.0.0.1, so http://0.0.0.0:<port>/ passes validateURL AND the dial-time re-check, reaching any local service the guard exists to block. The three-layer defence itself (pre-flight, redirect re-check, dial-time re-validation) is sound.

title: EPIC: memory/skill retrieval honesty
description: Small cluster: retrieval tools must report WHICH PATH ran and WHAT WAS WITHHELD, so empty recall means "not known", not "search was degraded". Instances: yaah-h4e (memory_search.md still does not disclose tag forces keyword-only FTS — the third surface of the old three-surface defect), yaah-17s (memory_search vector to FTS degradation unlabelled; vector error discarded — label the path like the sibling [semantic] output does), yaah-92p (skill semantic search has no relevance floor — every skill is reported as a match; per-skill embedding errors swallowed).

title: EPIC: docs from truth — verification not generation, one source of truth for arg semantics
description: MECHANISM (codegen/go:generate is BANNED by repo convention — so verification, not generation): THE DOC RULE: internal/prompts/tools/<tool>.md states BEHAVIOR and POLICY only; it must NOT restate argument semantics — the JSON schema description owns arg semantics and is the contract. This structurally deletes the worst lie class (read.md byte-offset, bisect test_cmd, patch.md file-path were all arg restatements). Parity test (core bead yaah-two7) enforces: every registered tool has a doc or an explicit exemption; every doc is referenced; every schema property name appears in its doc; claim tables asserted against code (git.md safe/mutating table vs allowedGitActions). proposal/supervisor stop bypassing the layer (inline Description strings) — add proposal.md + supervisor.md via prompts.ToolDescription. Instances: yaah-two7 (CORE: parity test), yaah-yf5 (read.md bytes vs lines), yaah-nxb (bisect test_cmd schema), yaah-k9x (go_mod dry_run canned preview), yaah-hae (go_refactor.md overstates), yaah-9h6 (bg list running claim), yaah-3lm (ls.md sizes + ignored-only empty), yaah-4mt (todowrite contract oversold), yaah-yo5 (list_subagents.md phantom model field), yaah-t8b (proposal/supervisor missing docs), yaah-bq2 (delegate timeout_seconds dead knob — schema/doc agreement), yaah-f36h (webfetch markdown claim), yaah-5ew (edit tautological comment — comments are docs too).

title: EPIC-A core: unify truncation policy + multiResult accumulator + conformance kit in internal/tools
description: The class fix behind 16 instance beads. Three pieces: (1) one truncation owner (unify helpers.go toolResultMaxLen/truncateOutput, replaceMaxResultLen, the webfetch copy, loop-level agent_truncation) with the invariant: error payloads and per-item failure lines are never truncated — failures are prepended so a cap can only eat success detail; (2) a tiny multiResult done/failed accumulator returning non-nil error on any failure (the pattern edit.go implements by hand); (3) internal/tools/conformance_test.go — table of failing scenarios per tool asserting err != nil. No ResultBuilder god-object; the rule "nil error means the operation succeeded" lives in the tools.go doc comment and the tests enforce it. See bd remember key tool-result-honesty.

title: EPIC-B core: source-scan enforcement — undeclared os/io.fs access in internal/tools fails the build
description: The class fix behind 10 instance beads. A test in the package scans internal/tools source for os/io.fs usage outside a declared allowlist; anything undeclared fails unless the tool is declared host-only via the existing isHostOnlyTool mechanism. Declared host-only is fine; undeclared os.* is a failure. Do NOT make WorkspaceSetter mandatory at the registry — the registry cannot know who touches the filesystem. See bd remember key tool-workspace-enforcement.

title: EPIC-D core: typed Outcome for settlement/lifecycle verbs (retained + subagent_jobs)
description: The class fix behind 8 instance beads. Settlement/lifecycle verbs return a typed Outcome {Work: landed|discarded|kept; Scope: intact|removed|stranded; Record: consumed|open; Notes: []string — never truncated, teardown failures land here} instead of one status word. Mirrors the typed-events architecture (errors are values). subagent_jobs borrows the shape: cancel reports cancelled/already finished/unknown; wait exposes still_running as a documented field instead of an invented timed_out status. See bd remember key tool-outcome-shape.

title: proposal registry: fail loudly when a runtime has no registry instead of a process-global fallback
description: Follow-up to yaah-yox (PR #597 review): defaultProposalRegistry (internal/tools/retained.go ~:129) backs zero-value RetainedRuntime/ProposalTool construction with a process-global registry, silently reintroducing cross-session proposal leakage if any composition path other than cmd/yaah wiring constructs the runtime. Consistent with errors-are-values, registry() should return nil and the tool should error 'proposal registry not configured' so an unwired composition fails loudly. Touches zero-value constructors and tests, hence a separate bead rather than widening #597.

title: compaction observability: record the summarizer call so failures are auditable after the fact
description: During the 2026-10-26 incident (yaah-v378) the compacted_summary in state.db proved the summary was the unfilled template, but the summarizer's raw request/response could not be audited: compactProvider.Send in context_manager.go is not traced, and trace.db only records sub-agent executions. Record the compaction execution (model, prompt size, excerpt size, response, rejection reason if any) in trace.db or the CompactionDoneEvent/state, redacted to size bounds. AC: after a compaction, one can answer 'what did the summarizer receive and return, and was it accepted?' from persisted data alone.

title: main-loop intent-repetition detector: steer when the assistant re-announces the same intent without a mutating action
description: The 2026-10-26 incident loop (yaah-v378): twelve consecutive assistant turns re-announced the same intent ('All four findings are real. Implementing now…') while issuing only 2-4 varied read calls per turn. loop_detection could not see it: the hard halt needs 5 IDENTICAL (tool,args,result) hashes in a 10-call window (commands varied slightly each turn), and the convergence nudge needs >=5 calls of one tool WITHIN one turn for 3 consecutive turns (each loop turn had 2-4). Add a cross-turn detector: hash a normalized assistant text prefix (strip backtick contents/numbers) and steer after N consecutive near-identical preambles with no mutating tool call (no edit/patch/write/proposal-settle class) in the window. Reuse the [STEER] injection shape from LoopDetectionMiddleware.PrepareStep. AC: a test replays the incident shape (N same-preamble turns with varied bash reads) and asserts a steer message is injected by turn N; a healthy investigate-then-edit sequence does not trigger it.

title: usage accounting: sessions on some surfaces record 0 tokens/0 usage despite real activity
description: Several sessions show tokens_in/out = 0 in state.db while real LLM activity happened: sess-1793070391 (2026-10-26 21:06-23:36, 150 min, 0 messages, 0 tokens) and sess-1793116553 (2026-10-27 09:55-10:02, 34 messages, 0 tokens — a live agent loop the user experienced). Both are believed to be ACP/Zed sessions; the TUI/REPL sessions of the same period record usage fine. Consequence: runaway-loop incidents are invisible in session totals — the 2026-10-26 loop (5.8M tokens) was only measurable because it ran on TUI. Investigate the OnUsage flush path and persister wiring for the ACP/serve surfaces (auxProviders/loopBuilder construction for acp_cmd), and whether message persistence also differs (150-min session with 0 messages persisted). AC: a test drives an ACP-shaped session and asserts usage rows and messages are persisted; sessions with real activity always show nonzero tokens_in.

title: summary rendering: /compact should render the produced summary in the conversation stream
description: opencode renders the compaction summary in the conversation stream; yaah emits only ephemeral status lines (TUI SetEphemeral, SSE ctrl.status, stderr) and ForceCompact returns nothing, so the user never sees what the summarizer produced — the 2026-10-26 empty-template summary (v378.1) would have been visible instantly. Design (agreed 2026-10-27): ForceCompact returns CompactionResult{Summary, Method, BeforeTokens, AfterTokens}; new control.CompactionSummary message; TUI renders a durable conversation-log card (control.Error pattern, not SetEphemeral); web gets a ctrl.compaction SSE event; ACP forwards an honestly-labeled session/update chunk; REPL prints the block on its stderr path. RENDER-ONLY: never persist the summary as a chat message (it already lives in the system message; a copy double-counts tokens). Trim fallback renders honestly as 'trimmed — no summary produced'.

title: EPIC: bench harness & evidence
description: Bench/eval harness work. Children: yaah-53i (OpenCode Terminal-Bench arm), yaah-vm9 (orch-recovery Terminal-Bench task), yaah-bpu (_mock 009 determinism track), yaah-5k6 (evidence-guard thresholds on harness traces).

title: EPIC: sub-agent efficiency & orchestration
description: Sub-agent dispatch cost and pipeline-contract fixes. Children: yaah-car (nested delegation cost), yaah-csg (sibling result re-reads), yaah-ehf (no result memoization), yaah-9bq (overlapping speculation all-or-nothing), yaah-awn (nonstandard tool-call dialects), yaah-b56 (supervised_task ErrNoSandbox), yaah-iw4 (nudge middleware), yaah-cga (dormant hooks integration).

title: EPIC: provider/LLM protocol robustness
description: Wire-protocol and accounting fixes on the provider boundary. Children: yaah-31j (fallback reasoning-format mismatch), yaah-n7k (json_mode hardcoded), yaah-d9b0 (zero-token usage accounting), yaah-eyh (validators bypass the LLM semaphore), yaah-rza (resume msg conversation_id ignores provider).

title: EPIC: embedding/probe honesty (xyx4 follow-ups)
description: Follow-ups to the closed yaah-xyx4 memory/skill retrieval honesty epic. Children: yaah-shq (memory_search drops 384-dim embeddings when tag is set), yaah-ka6 (surface embedder probe/model mismatch as a warning).

title: EPIC: sandbox containment backends
description:
Containment mechanism work, kept separate from yaah-lvsj (which is about enforcement policy by construction). Children: yaah-mct (Windows winacl containment), yaah-1tkp.1 (sub-agent shell guard is tool-granular - denies powershell wholesale, no read-only allowlist), yaah-1tkp.2 (developer lane cannot execute go_test/staticcheck, so proposals land unverified), yaah-kit (goatherd sandbox seam), yaah-bp4 (retire the gitsandbox decorator).

Interim policy while 1tkp.1 and 1tkp.2 are open: a proposal from a lane that could not execute is never committed as-is - the parent selects it onto a scratch branch and runs go build ./..., go test ./..., gofmt -l ., go vet and staticcheck first, and treats all contract evidence fields from that lane as absent.

title: memory_search: tag filter silently degrades to keyword-only FTS, losing recall on natural-language queries
description:
Reproduced 2026-10-27 in a live harness session during a memory capability test.

SYMPTOM: memory_search with a tag filter returns 'No matching memories found' for queries that the same search WITHOUT the tag answers correctly.

REPRODUCTION (two probes over the same store):
- query='CLI audit method', tag=['project:yaah']  -> 0 hits
- query='CLI audit' (no tag)                      -> 3 hits, including the CLI-audit atoms

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, high confidence): supplying a tag silently drops the embedding/vector path and falls back to FTS5 keyword-only matching. The default FTS5 tokenizer does not stem, so the AND query cli AND audit AND method misses an atom containing 'Method for AUDITING yaah's CLI surface' ('audit' != 'auditing'). The untagged path answers via semantic embeddings and succeeds.

NOTE: epic yaah-xyx4 (CLOSED) addressed the DISCLOSURE surface (yaah-h4e doc/schema parity, yaah-17s label the degradation, yaah-92p relevance floor) — see close reason: children landed on feat/memory-retrieval-honesty (local commits, not pushed). This bead is the remaining BEHAVIOR defect behind that disclosure: retrieval with a tag is materially worse than retrieval without one, so tagging an atom makes it harder to find.

POSSIBLE FIX DIRECTIONS (open to design):
1. Don't drop the vector path when a tag is present — filter semantic results by tag post-hoc (tag as a filter, not a path selector).
2. If keyword-only is intentional for tag queries, at least OR-expand / stem tokens, and surface a 'keyword-only path' label + recall caveat in the result (consistent with yaah-17s's labeling work).

ACCEPTANCE: the repro pair above returns the CLI-audit atoms with the tag present; any remaining path degradation is labelled in the tool output.

title: github_get_file_contents returns success with no file content; 're-run the tool' hint is a no-op loop
description:
Observed while analyzing StarTrail-org/LEANN: github_get_file_contents(/README.md) -- a 53,613-byte file -- delivered NO file content. The call reported success and the only text that reached the model was a pruning notice:

  [output pruned - 81 chars omitted to save context; re-run the tool if you need it again]

The same call shape on the repo root (/README-adjacent listing) returned "[output pruned - 1239 chars omitted to save context; ...]". In both cases the model received zero bytes of the actual payload. Recovery required falling back to webfetch against raw.githubusercontent.com.

Two distinct defects:

1. SUCCESS-WITH-NO-CONTENT. A file-read tool must either deliver the body or return an error naming why not. A success frame whose payload is entirely replaced by a pruning notice is exactly the "tool results must not lie" failure that yaah-ebqk was about.

2. THE REMEDY HINT IS A NO-OP LOOP. "re-run the tool if you need it again" is false for a deterministic read: re-invoking returns the identical pruned frame. There is no follow-up affordance (offset/limit, spill path, or a legible error) that reaches the content.

NOTES / possible cause: 81 chars is consistent with the upstream GitHub MCP server returning a "successfully downloaded text file (SHA: ...)" style stub for files it will not inline; the stub is then pruned by the output pruner, so the model sees neither the body nor the notice. Unconfirmed from the harness side -- instrument whether the pruned payload was the file body or a download stub before choosing the fix.

EVIDENCE: session 1793199936214646200; tool result text quoted verbatim above; webfetch fallback succeeded on the same path.

title: Sub-agent lane denies powershell wholesale ('Blocked destructive operation') -- no read-only shell for analysis
description:
Every powershell call made by a dispatched analyst sub-agent was denied:

  error: tool "powershell" denied by supervisor guard: Blocked destructive operation (powershell). Supervisor denied.

This was not a blocked command -- the guard rejected the tool by name for every invocation, including pure reads. The parent lane, running the same class of command in the same session, was not denied, so the policy diverges by lane with no documented reason.

CONSEQUENCE: two analyst sub-agents surveying a codebase and its ecosystem could not clone a repo, run go list or git ls-files, measure file or shared-library sizes, or run cloc. Every size- and presence-related figure in their reports had to come back "estimated" or "unverified": they walked directory trees one REST call at a time and cross-checked byte sums by hand. Two concrete degradations this session: (a) LEANN's exact repo-wide file count is unknown; (b) Go ONNX / llama.cpp shared-library sizes in MB are approximations that a single Get-Item would have settled.

ROOT ISSUE: the guard is tool-granular where it needs to be command-granular. A read-only allowlist (git clone into a temp dir, git ls-files, go list, Get-ChildItem/du, wc, cloc, --version probes) covers the analytical use case while still blocking mutation. Note that the denial text does not name the offending command or the matched rule, so the sub-agent cannot self-correct or report what it was trying to do.

title: providers: decode array-shaped delta.content blocks; GLM reasoning silently dropped
description:
zai-glm-5-3 (and GLM models on Mistral generally) stream delta.content as an ARRAY of typed blocks, not a string:

  {"delta":{"content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":[{"type":"text","text":"The"}],"closed":true}]}}

providers.StreamDelta.Content is a string, so parseSSEChunk (internal/providers/stream.go) returns a json.Unmarshal error and SendStream silently `continue`s - the chunk is dropped with no log and no counter. Result: all reasoning text is lost, invisible in the UI and in traces. Text deltas are plain strings, so final answers still render (verified: a live zai-glm-5-3 one-shot replies "pong" while emitting zero reasoning).

Fix: make StreamDelta.Content accept both shapes - either a custom UnmarshalJSON treating a decoded string as text and
  * {"type":"thinking",...} blocks as reasoning (mapping onto ReasoningContent), with text blocks mapping onto Content,
  * or a json.RawMessage/union type normalized at parse time.
Also stop dropping undecodable chunks silently: log/trace them (once per turn, rate-limited) so a future wire-shape change is visible instead of looking like a model with no reasoning.

Evidence: raw SSE captured from POST https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions {"model":"zai-glm-5-3","stream":true}.

title: EPIC: Shepherd parity closure — remaining divergences
description:
# Shepherd parity closure

Shepherd parity is largely done on the invariants that matter: the frozen kernel
ABI is byte-identical, retained outputs and consume-once settlement ship for
local sessions, and Linux/Windows enforce containment natively. What remains is
spread across three unrelated epics and, in two cases, tracked nowhere. This
epic is the single owner of the remaining divergences. Mechanism work stays in
the goatherd modules; yaah children here are either implementations or tracking
links to upstream beads.

## Closed / deliberately out of scope

- **Kernel ABI** — 100%, frozen (goatherd-kernel v0.18.0, golden vectors against
  Python shepherd pin `d34d5ca`).
- **Retained outputs + settlement** — shipped (`delegate`, `proposal
  select/apply/release/discard`, report lane).
- **Enforcement policy by construction** — `yaah-lvsj`, closed 2026-10-28.
- **TaskControl (D6) and materialize receipts (D7)** — deliberate bypasses;
  the upstream decision is `shepherd-runtime-go-s3u`.

## Children

1. macOS Seatbelt backend — the last native enforcement hole.
2. Per-binding read/write grants compiled to multi-root confinement.
3. Retained outputs + settlement for container sessions (croft-dlb blocker).
4. Decision: retain top-level session runs?
5. Parity ledger: refresh the gap report and pin it with a drift guard.

## Related, separately owned

- `yaah-1tkp` containment mechanisms: `yaah-mct` and the adapter half of
  `yaah-kit` have shipped; close or re-scope both once verified.
- `yaah-sx7h` bench harness (results parity), `yaah-95ri` sub-agent efficiency.

## Exit criteria

Every row of the parity scorecard in `yaah-shepherd-gap-report.md` is shipped,
explicitly declined, or owned by a bead with a verification test; the report
matches the current module names and pins.

title: feat(permissions): per-binding read/write grants compiled to multi-root confinement
description:
# Per-binding permission grants compiled to multi-root confinement

## Context

Shepherd declares authority in the signature: `repo: GitRepo`, `May[GitRepo,
ReadOnly]`, `May[GitRepo, ReadWrite]`. Unannotated parameters carry no ambient
write authority, and the annotations lower into multi-root confinement rules.

yaah has no signature DSL. A sub-agent is granted one `ReadWrite` root — its
isolated worktree. Adjacent axes were narrowed since the audit (per-role tool
belts, egress postures, argument-aware danger, Workspace-only FS access via
`yaah-lvsj`), but there is still no per-binding, multi-root filesystem compile.
This is the largest conceptual divergence left.

## Plan

1. Decide the surface: role/dispatch config plus tool declarations, or a
   DSL-ish annotation layer. It must survive tool registration; do not make the
   registry responsible for filesystem knowledge (see `yaah-lvsj`).
2. Compile declarations into confinement roots with rights (RW/RO) and
   deny-by-default for undeclared paths. Unknown or non-existent roots fail
   loudly rather than widening.
3. Support read-only roots, including the parent repo or `.git` where a role
   needs read but not write. Today the single root cannot express that at all.
4. Refuse what the platform cannot enforce rather than silently narrowing or
   widening; advisory runs record exactly which grants went unenforced.
5. Tests: RO root write denied, RW root write allowed, undeclared path denied,
   disjoint multi-root, Linux and Windows parity, advisory honesty.
6. Document the model in `docs/configuration.md` and the sub-agent prompt
   guidance.

## Acceptance

- A role can declare two roots with different rights and the jail enforces the
  difference on Linux and Windows.
- Undeclared paths are denied, never implicitly granted.
- The config surface rejects unknown roots and unsupported rights at load time.
- No role gains write authority through tool registration alone.

title: feat(container): retained outputs and settlement for container sessions
description:
# Retained outputs and settlement for container sessions

## Context

Container sessions now flow through the goatherd sandbox seam (`sandbox/croft`
adapter, yaah `afcbc94`), but `Retain` is still gated on `sessionSandbox == nil`
in `cmd/yaah/wiring.go`. Container runs produce no retained output and cannot
settle.

The reason is real: settlement's `select` precondition compares
`trace.WorkspaceState` digests as content equality, and croft states are
sequence-keyed — re-capturing unchanged content yields a new key and a new
digest. **Hard blocker: `croft-dlb`** (no-change capture fast path + exposed
content digest) in goatherd-croft. This is Phase 3 of `yaah-kit` and was
deliberately left out of that bead's scope.

## Plan

1. Land `croft-dlb`; confirm a no-change recapture digests equally through the
   adapter's `Capture`.
2. Enable capture/apply on the container lane and map the verbs:
   `select` -> capture on parent when unmoved; `apply` -> `ApplyDelta`, failing
   closed on `ErrDeltaConflict`; `release` -> keep the pinned state; `discard`
   -> destroy.
3. Revisit recovery/adoption. Croft identity is not a path, so `Addressed` stays
   unimplemented; container recovery remains a recorded follow-up, not a silent

- Two captures of unchanged content digest equally; `select` never misfires.

title: ACP: session modes (Plan/Build) — advertise modes, honor session/set_mode, emit current_mode_update
description:
ACP Session Modes (Plan/Build): advertise modes, honor session/set_mode, emit current_mode_update.

## Why

ACP models agent modes (e.g. Zed's Plan/Build picker) as "Session Modes"
(agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-modes; v1 schema defs SessionMode,
SessionModeState, SetSessionModeRequest, SetSessionModeResponse,
CurrentModeUpdate). Clients render the picker from the `modes` state returned
by session/new (and load/resume/fork), switch via session/set_mode
{sessionId, modeId}, and receive CurrentModeUpdate {currentModeId} as a
session/update when the mode changes (including tool-driven switches; there
is a `switch_mode` tool kind for that).

yaah today only acknowledges session/set_mode (internal/acp/server.go
handleSetMode ~line 1244: "Modes are not modeled") and session/new returns
no `modes`, so clients show no picker and the TCK's capability-inferred
modes tests (inferred:modes, tck/v1/requirements.py ~573/593) SKIP with
"session/new returned no modes/configOptions".

## Scope

1. Advertise modes: session/new, session/load, and session/resume responses
   gain `modes: SessionModeState{currentModeId, availableModes}` — at least
   `build` (default) and `plan`, each with name + description.
2. Honor session/set_mode: validate modeId (unknown id = JSON-RPC error,
   not silent success; SetSessionModeResponse is empty on success), then
   switch session behavior via existing seams — plan = read-only tool set
   (ToolsLevel) + planning directive; build = normal operation.
3. Emit CurrentModeUpdate on every mode change (transport: session/update
   variant current_mode_update), including future tool-driven switches via
   the switch_mode tool kind.
4. Decide + document mode persistence: either persist the current mode on
   the session row so load/resume restore it, or re-default to `build` on
   resume. Pick one and pin it in tests.
5. Tests: transport tests for modes in session/new+load+resume results,
   set_mode flipping tool visibility per session, current_mode_update
   emission, unknown-mode error; TCK inferred:modes rows must move from
   SKIP to PASS (57 passed / 17 skipped baseline, acp-serve).
6. Docs: docs/acp.md — replace the "session/set_mode | acknowledged" row
   with real behavior and document the mode list in the session/new
   section; features.md if the modes are user-visible.

## Notes

- Base on current main: the repo refactored since v0.96 (internal/sessions/
  registry, internal/cwdpath/, `yaah mcp serve` replaces `yaah serve --http`).
- v1 mode tests are capability-inferred (draft: docs/protocol/v1/draft/
  session-modes.mdx): only exercised when session/new returns non-null modes.
- SystemPromptMode (client-provided system prompts) is a separate UNSTABLE
  capability — out of scope here.
- There is no mode parameter on NewSessionRequest in v1: the initial mode is
  whatever the agent reports as currentModeId; clients switch afterwards.

## Acceptance

A mode-aware client shows a Plan/Build picker for yaah, session/set_mode
switches the tool level live for that session, current_mode_update is
emitted on change, TCK inferred:modes tests pass, docs match behavior.
